至于红钩区——它总是老样子。苏伊达姆来了又去了；一场恐怖聚了又散了；可黑暗与污秽的邪灵，依旧孵在老砖房里的杂种们中间，游荡的帮伙仍在不明差事上巡行，走过一扇扇窗，窗里的灯火与扭曲的脸孔无端地显了又没。太古的恐怖是一头千首的水螅；黑暗的诸教团，根扎在比德谟克利特之井更深的渎神里。兽的灵魂无处不在，而且得胜；红钩区那些眼泡浮肿、麻脸的大军，仍在诵、在咒、在嚎，鱼贯从一个深渊行向另一个深渊，没人知道从哪来往哪去，只被他们永远理解不了的盲目的生物学法则推着。同旧日一样，进红钩区的人比从陆路出去的多；已有风声，说新的沟渠又在地下伸展，通向几处酒和更不好提名目的东西的集散地。

那座舞厅教堂如今大体还是舞厅，夜里有怪脸在窗口出现。近来有个警察放话，说填死的地穴又被挖开了，而且图的不为什么简单的名目。毒物比历史和人类还要古老，我们又拿什么去扑打？猿猴在亚洲就朝着那些恐怖跳过舞；而今，鬼祟藏身在一排排朽坏的砖房里，癌瘤安然而蔓延。

马隆打寒噤不是没有来由——就在前几天，一名警员听见一个踢黑的斜眼老妪，在一条巷道的荫翳里教一个小娃娃某种咬耳朵的土话。他听了一阵，觉得古怪至极，因为听见她翻来覆去念的是：

「黑夜的朋友与同侣啊，你以犬吠与溅血为乐，你出没于坟茔之间的幽影之中，你渴血而使凡人恐怖——戈耳戈，莫尔莫，千面的月啊，垂青我们的祭飨！」

## The Hound / 猎犬
===Original===



===Chinese===

猎犬

### I / 一
===Original===

In my tortured ears there sounds unceasingly a nightmare whirring and flapping, and a faint, distant baying as of some gigantic hound. It is not dream﻿—it is not, I fear, even madness﻿—for too much has already happened to give me these merciful doubts.

St. John is a mangled corpse; I alone know why, and such is my knowledge that I am about to blow out my brains for fear I shall be mangled in the same way. Down unlit and illimitable corridors of eldritch fantasy sweeps the black, shapeless Nemesis that drives me to self-annihilation.

May heaven forgive the folly and morbidity which led us both to so monstrous a fate! Wearied with the commonplaces of a prosaic world, where even the joys of romance and adventure soon grow stale, St. John and I had followed enthusiastically every aesthetic and intellectual movement which promised respite from our devastating ennui. The enigmas of the symbolists and the ecstasies of the pre-Raphaelites all were ours in their time, but each new mood was drained too soon of its diverting novelty and appeal.

Only the sombre philosophy of the decadents could hold us, and this we found potent only by increasing gradually the depth and diabolism of our penetrations. Baudelaire and Huysmans were soon exhausted of thrills, till finally there remained for us only the more direct stimuli of unnatural personal experiences and adventures. It was this frightful emotional need which led us eventually to that detestable course which even in my present fear I mention with shame and timidity﻿—that hideous extremity of human outrage, the abhorred practice of grave-robbing.

===Chinese===

在我受尽折磨的耳中，无休无止地响着一场梦魇似的呼呼振翅与扑打，还有一阵微弱而遥远的狂吠，仿佛出自某头巨犬。这不是梦——我恐怕，甚至也不是疯狂——因为已经发生的事情太多了，多到不容我再抱这两种慈悲的疑念。

圣约翰已是一具血肉模糊的尸体；唯独我知道缘故，而正因这份知，我即将轰掉自己的脑袋，唯恐也落得同样被撕碎的下场。在鬼怪幻想那无灯而无尽的走廊里，一团漆黑、无形的复仇之神一路横扫，把我驱向自我了断。

愿上天宽恕那把我们两个都引到如此骇人下场的愚妄与病态！我们厌倦了散文世界里的平庸陈腐——在那里，就连罗曼司与冒险的欢乐也很快变得陈旧——圣约翰和我便满怀热忱地追逐过每一场许诺把我们从毁灭性的倦怠里解救出来的审美与智识运动。象征主义者的谜语、前拉斐尔派的狂喜，我们都曾先后领有；但每一种新情调，那份消遣的新奇与魅力，都太早就被吮吸干了。

唯有颓废派的阴郁哲学还留得住我们，而它也只有在我们的钻探步步加深、愈见邪恶时，才显出效力。波德莱尔与于斯曼很快就叫我们耗尽了战栗，到最后，留给我们的只剩下更直接的刺激：不自然的亲身经历与冒险。正是这种可怕的情感饥渴，最终把我们引上了那条可憎的路——即便在此刻的恐惧里，我提起它来仍然又羞又怯——那人性暴行的骇人极端，人人痛绝的盗墓行当。

===Original===

I cannot reveal the details of our shocking expeditions, or catalogue even partly the worst of the trophies adorning the nameless museum we prepared in the great stone house where we jointly dwelt, alone and servantless. Our museum was a blasphemous, unthinkable place, where with the satanic taste of neurotic virtuosi we had assembled an universe of terror and decay to excite our jaded sensibilities. It was a secret room, far, far underground; where huge winged daemons carven of basalt and onyx vomited from wide grinning mouths weird green and orange light, and hidden pneumatic pipes ruffled into kaleidoscopic dances of death the lines of red charnel things hand in hand woven on voluminous black hangings. Through these pipes came at will the odors our moods most craved; sometimes the scent of pale funereal lilies, sometimes the narcotic incense of imagined Eastern shrines of the kingly dead, and sometimes﻿—how I shudder to recall it!﻿—the frightful, soul-upheaving stenches of the uncovered grave.

Around the walls of this repellent chamber were cases of antique mummies alternating with comely, lifelike bodies perfectly stuffed and cured by the taxidermist’s art, and with headstones snatched from the oldest churchyards of the world. Niches here and there contained skulls of all shapes, and heads preserved in various stages of dissolution. There one might find the rotting, bald pates of famous noblemen, and the fresh and radiantly golden heads of new-buried children.

Statues and paintings there were, all of fiendish subjects and some executed by St. John and myself. A locked portfolio, bound in tanned human skin, held certain unknown and unnamable drawings which it was rumored Goya had perpetrated but dared not acknowledge. There were nauseous musical instruments, stringed, brass, and woodwind, on which St. John and I sometimes produced dissonances of exquisite morbidity and cacodaemoniacal ghastliness; whilst in a multitude of inlaid ebony cabinets reposed the most incredible and unimaginable variety of tomb-loot ever assembled by human madness and perversity. It is of this loot in particular that I must not speak﻿—thank God I had the courage to destroy it long before I thought of destroying myself!

---

===Chinese===

我们那些骇人听闻的出征，细节无可奉告；我们共同栖身的那座石头大宅里有一间无名的博物馆，里面陈设的战利品，哪怕只把最不堪的开列个大概，也办不到。我们的博物馆是一个渎神的、不可思议的地方：怀着神经质的鉴赏家的魔鬼趣味，我们在其中集结了一个恐怖与朽烂的宇宙，来撩动我们疲惫的感官。那是一间密室，深深、深深地藏在地下；巨大的、雕成玄武岩与缟玛瑙的有翼恶魔，从咧开的阔嘴里喷吐出诡异的绿光与橙光，暗藏的气管把黑沉沉的巨幅帷幔吹得波动起伏——上面手拉手织成的红色藏尸间的图案，便跳起万花筒般的死亡之舞。凭着这些管道，我们心境最渴求的香气可以随意送来：有时是苍白的丧仪百合的芬芳，有时是想象中东方王陵神殿那催眠似的熏香，有时——回想起来我仍浑身发抖！——是那掀开的坟墓里骇人的、掀翻灵魂的恶臭。

这间令人作呕的屋子四壁，陈列柜里古代的木乃伊与美观逼真、经标本师妙手填充保存的尸身相间而立，还有从世界上最古老的教堂墓园里抢来的墓碑。壁龛错落，里面供着各种形状的颅骨，和保存到腐烂各个阶段的头颅。在那里，可以看见名门显贵腐烂的秃头，也能看见新葬孩子的容光焕发的金色头颅。

还有雕像和绘画，题材无一不是恶魔，有几件出自圣约翰和我本人之手。一部上了锁的对开本，用人皮鞣制装帧，收着若干无名可称的画——传闻是戈雅的手笔，只是他不敢认领。那里有令人作呕的乐器，弦乐、铜管、木管，圣约翰和我有时在它们上面奏出精妙的病态与恶魔般阴惨的不谐和音；而一具具镶嵌乌木的柜子里，安放着人类疯狂与悖德所能搜罗到的最不可思议、最难以想象的盗墓赃物。正是这批赃物，我尤其不可提及——感谢上帝，早在我想到了结自己之前很久，我就有勇气把它们毁掉了！

===Original===

The predatory excursions on which we collected our unmentionable treasures were always artistically memorable events. We were no vulgar ghouls, but worked only under certain conditions of mood, landscape, environment, weather, season, and moonlight. These pastimes were to us the most exquisite form of aesthetic expression, and we gave their details a fastidious technical care. An inappropriate hour, a jarring lighting effect, or a clumsy manipulation of the damp sod, would almost totally destroy for us that ecstatic titillation which followed the exhumation of some ominous, grinning secret of the earth. Our quest for novel scenes and piquant conditions was feverish and insatiate﻿—St. John was always the leader, and he it was who led the way at last to that mocking, accursed spot which brought us our hideous and inevitable doom.

By what malign fatality were we lured to that terrible Holland churchyard? I think it was the dark rumor and legendry, the tales of one buried for five centuries, who had himself been a ghoul in his time and had stolen a potent thing from a mighty sepulchre. I can recall the scene in these final moments﻿—the pale autumnal moon over the graves, casting long horrible shadows; the grotesque trees, drooping sullenly to meet the neglected grass and the crumbling slabs; the vast legions of strangely colossal bats that flew against the moon; the antique ivied church pointing a huge spectral finger at the livid sky; the phosphorescent insects that danced like death-fires under the yews in a distant corner; the odors of mould, vegetation, and less explicable things that mingled feebly with the night-wind from over far swamps and seas; and, worst of all, the faint deep-toned baying of some gigantic hound which we could neither see nor definitely place. As we heard this suggestion of baying we shuddered, remembering the tales of the peasantry; for he whom we sought had centuries before been found in this selfsame spot, torn and mangled by the claws and teeth of some unspeakable beast.

===Chinese===

我们出门搜罗那些不可名状之宝的掠夺性远征，桩桩都是艺术上值得纪念的大事。我们不是庸俗的食尸鬼，只在心境、风景、环境、天气、季节与月光种种条件俱备时动手。这类消遣于我们是最高妙的美学表达形式，其细节我们以一丝不苟的技艺悉心经营。时辰不当，光效不谐，或者翻动湿土时手上一个笨拙，都会几乎彻底毁掉那从地下掘出某个狞笑的不祥秘密之后的销魂震颤。我们对新奇场景与刺激条件的寻求狂热而不知餍足——领头的总是圣约翰，也正是他，最终把我们引到了那个讥诮的、受诅咒的地点，给我们带来骇人而不可避免的厄运。

究竟是哪一种恶毒的命运，把我们诱到那座可怕的荷兰教堂墓园？我想，是那些黑暗的传闻与野史——关于一个下葬已五百年的人，他生前自己就是个食尸鬼，曾从一座威严的陵墓里偷过一件法力强大的东西。在这最后的时刻，我还记得那情景：苍白的秋月悬在坟头，投下长长的可怖的影；怪模怪样的树阴沉地垂向无人照管的荒草与崩裂的石板；成群结队、大得出奇的蝙蝠列成浩荡军容扑过月亮；爬满常春藤的古教堂向青白的天空指着一条巨大的鬼魅手指；磷光闪烁的虫子像鬼火一样在远处角落的紫杉下跳舞；霉、草木和更难解释的东西的气味，同远自沼泽与海面吹来的夜风微弱地混在一起；而最糟的是，某头巨犬那低沉而隐约的吠声，我们既看不见，也定不了方位。听见这似有似无的吠声，我们打了个寒噤，想起乡民的传说；因为我们寻觅的那个人，几百年前正是在这同一个地点被人发现的，被某种不可名状的野兽的爪牙撕得稀烂。

===Original===

I remember how we delved in this ghoul’s grave with our spades, and how we thrilled at the picture of ourselves, the grave, the pale watching moon, the horrible shadows, the grotesque trees, the titanic bats, the antique church, the dancing death-fires, the sickening odors, the gently moaning night-wind, and the strange, half-heard, directionless baying, of whose objective existence we could scarcely be sure.

Then we struck a substance harder than the damp mould, and beheld a rotting oblong box crusted with mineral deposits from the long undisturbed ground. It was incredibly tough and thick, but so old that we finally pried it open and feasted our eyes on what it held.

Much﻿—amazingly much﻿—was left of the object despite the lapse of five hundred years. The skeleton, though crushed in places by the jaws of the thing that had killed it, held together with surprising firmness, and we gloated over the clean white skull with its long, firm teeth and its eyeless sockets that once had glowed with a charnel fever like our own. In the coffin lay an amulet of curious and exotic design, which had apparently been worn around the sleeper’s neck. It was the oddly conventionalised figure of a crouching winged hound, or sphinx with a semi-canine face, and was exquisitely carved in antique Oriental fashion from a small piece of green jade. The expression on its features was repellent in the extreme, savoring at once of death, bestiality, and malevolence. Around the base was an inscription in characters which neither St. John nor I could identify; and on the bottom, like a maker’s seal, was graven a grotesque and formidable skull.

===Chinese===

我记得我们怎样用铲子掘开这食尸鬼的坟，记得我们为自己勾勒出的这幅图画怎样令我们战栗：这座坟，惨白注视的月亮，可怖的影，怪树，巨蝠，古教堂，跳舞的鬼火，令人作呕的气味，低吟的夜风，还有那似听见又没听见、辨不出方向的吠声——它是否客观存在，我们几乎不敢断定。

随后铲子碰上了比湿土更硬的东西，露出一具朽烂的长方形匣子，结满了久无人扰的土地里析出的矿物质。它坚硬厚实得出奇，但终究太老了，我们终于撬开了它，饱看它盛着的东西。

五百年过去，那东西居然还剩下许多——多得惊人。骸骨虽然有些地方被杀死它的那张嘴咬碎了，却出奇坚固地连缀在一起；我们饱览那颗洁净的白颅骨，长长的、坚实的牙齿，和那空空的眼窝——眼窝当年曾经燃着藏尸热病似的火光，一如我们自己的眼睛。棺中有一枚护符，设计古怪而带着异域气息，显然是死者生前贴颈佩戴的。那是一个风格古怪程式化的蹲踞的有翼猎犬，或者说长着半犬面孔的斯芬克斯，用一小块绿玉按古代东方的式样精雕而成。它面上的表情穷凶极恶地可憎，兼有死亡、兽性与怨毒。底座一周刻着圣约翰和我都辨识不出的文字；底部像个制作者的印玺，雕着一颗狰狞的骷髅。

===Original===

Immediately upon beholding this amulet we knew that we must possess it: that this treasure alone was our logical pelf from the centuried grave. Even had its outlines been unfamiliar we would have desired it, but as we looked more closely we saw that it was not wholly unfamiliar. Alien it indeed was to all art and literature which sane and balanced readers know, but we recognized it as the thing hinted of in the forbidden *Necronomicon* of the mad Arab Abdul Alhazred; the ghastly soul-symbol of the corpse-eating cult of inaccessible Leng, in Central Asia. All too well did we trace the sinister lineaments described by the old Arab daemonologist; lineaments, he wrote, drawn from some obscure supernatural manifestation of the souls of those who vexed and gnawed at the dead.

Seizing the green jade object, we gave a last glance at the bleached and cavern-eyed face of its owner and closed up the grave as we found it. As we hastened from that abhorrent spot, the stolen amulet in St. John’s pocket, we thought we saw the bats descend in a body to the earth we had so lately rifled, as if seeking for some cursed and unholy nourishment. But the autumn moon shone weak and pale, and we could not be sure.

So, too, as we sailed the next day away from Holland to our home, we thought we heard the faint distant baying of some gigantic hound in the background. But the autumn wind moaned sad and wan, and we could not be sure.

===Chinese===

一看见这枚护符，我们就知道必须占有它：唯有这件珍宝，才算我们这趟世纪古坟之行合乎逻辑的赃获。即便它的形貌陌生，我们也必然渴望它；而仔细看去，它又并非全然陌生。它当然不见于神志清明、心态平和的读者所知的任何艺术与文学，但我们认出了它——疯狂的阿拉伯人阿卜杜尔·阿尔哈兹莱德那部禁忌的《死灵之书》里曾暗示过它；它是中亚那不可抵达的冷原（Leng）上食尸教派的骇人的魂灵符。老阿拉伯的恶魔学家描摹过的那副不祥的形貌，我们追认得分毫不差；他写道，那形貌取自某些纠缠、啃噬死者的魂灵的幽晦超自然显形。

我们抓起这枚绿玉的东西，朝它主人那张白森森、眼窝深陷的脸看了最后一眼，把坟墓照原样填好。离开那个可憎的地点时，护符揣在圣约翰衣袋里；我们仿佛看见蝙蝠成群扑落到我们方才劫掠过的土地上，像在寻觅某种受了诅咒、亵渎的滋养。但秋月苍白乏力，我们不敢断定。

同样，第二天我们扬帆离开荷兰回家时，仿佛也听见背后有某头巨犬隐隐的、遥远的吠声。但秋风呜咽，愁惨而无力，我们不敢断定。

### II / 二
===Original===

Less than a week after our return to England, strange things began to happen. We lived as recluses; devoid of friends, alone, and without servants in a few rooms of an ancient manor-house on a bleak and unfrequented moor; so that our doors were seldom disturbed by the knock of the visitor.

Now, however, we were troubled by what seemed to be frequent fumblings in the night, not only around the doors but around the windows also, upper as well as lower. Once we fancied that a large, opaque body darkened the library window when the moon was shining against it, and another time we thought we heard a whirring or flapping sound not far off. On each occasion investigation revealed nothing, and we began to ascribe the occurrences to imagination alone﻿—that same curiously disturbed imagination which still prolonged in our ears the faint far baying we thought we had heard in the Holland churchyard. The jade amulet now reposed in a niche in our museum, and sometimes we burned strangely scented candles before it. We read much in Alhazred’s *Necronomicon* about its properties, and about the relation of ghosts’ souls to the objects it symbolized; and were disturbed by what we read.

Then terror came.

On the night of September 24, 19﻿—, I heard a knock at my chamber door. Fancying it St. John’s, I bade the knocker enter, but was answered only by a shrill laugh. There was no one in the corridor. When I aroused St. John from his sleep, he professed entire ignorance of the event, and became as worried as I. It was that night that the faint, distant baying over the moor became to us a certain and dreaded reality.

Four day a later, whilst we were both in the hidden museum, there came a low, cautious scratching at the single door which led to the secret library staircase. Our alarm was now divided, for, besides our fear of the unknown, we had always entertained a dread that our grisly collection might be discovered. Extinguishing all lights, we proceeded to the door and threw it suddenly open; whereupon we felt an unaccountable rush of air, and heard, as if receding far away, a queer combination of rustling, tittering, and articulate chatter. Whether we were mad, dreaming, or in our senses, we did not try to determine. We only realized, with the blackest of apprehensions, that the apparently disembodied chatter was beyond a doubt *in the Dutch language*.

===Chinese===

回到英格兰不到一个星期，怪事开始发生了。我们深居简出：无亲无故，孤零零没有仆人，住在荒凉而人迹不至的荒原上一座古老庄园的几个房间里；我们的门很少被访客敲响。

然而现在，我们被夜里频频的摸索声搅得不安宁，不但在门边，也在窗边，楼上楼下都是。有一回，月光正照着图书室的窗，我们恍忽觉得一具巨大而不透光的身体遮暗了它；又有一回，我们仿佛听见不远处一种呼呼的振翅声。每一次查探都一无所获，我们渐渐把这些归因于纯粹的想象——正是那种奇怪地受着搅扰的想象，还把我们在荷兰墓园里自以为听见的那阵微弱遥远的犬吠，延续在我们的耳中。碧玉护符如今供在博物馆的一个壁龛里，我们有时在它面前点上气味奇特的蜡烛。我们在阿尔哈兹莱德的《死灵之书》里读到许多关于它的特性、关于亡魂与它所象征之物之关系的话，读得心中不宁。

随后恐怖降临了。

9月24日夜里，19——年，我听见敲我房门的声音。我以为是圣约翰，便叫门外的人进来，回答我的却只有一声尖利的笑。走廊里空无一人。我叫醒圣约翰，他对这事全然不知，也同我一样不安起来。正是那一夜，荒原上那微弱而遥远的犬吠，在我们听来成了确凿而可怖的现实。

四天后，我们俩正待在密室博物馆里，通往秘密楼梯的那扇独门上响起一阵低低的、小心翼翼的抓挠。此刻我们的惊惶一分为二：既怕那未知之物，又一直怕我们那批可怕的收藏被人发现。我们熄了所有的灯，摸到门边，猛地拉开门；登时感到一阵莫名其妙的疾风扑面，还听见——仿佛在远远退去——一阵古怪的声音，窸窣、窃笑与清晰的话语混作一团。我们是疯了、在做梦、还是清醒着，我们没有去分辨。我们只是怀着最黑的预感意识到：那显然不依附于身体的话语，分明确凿是荷兰语。

===Original===

After that we lived in growing horror and fascination. Mostly we held to the theory that we were jointly going mad from our life of unnatural excitements, but sometimes it pleased us more to dramatize ourselves as the victims of some creeping and appalling doom. Bizarre manifestations were now too frequent to count. Our lonely house was seemingly alive with the presence of some malign being whose nature we could not guess, and every night that daemoniac baying rolled over the windswept moor, always louder and louder. On October 29 we found in the soft earth underneath the library window a series of footprints utterly impossible to describe. They were as baffling as the hordes of great bats which haunted the old manor-house in unprecedented and increasing numbers.

The horror reached a culmination on November 18, when St. John, walking home after dark from the dismal railway station, was seized by some frightful carnivorous thing and torn to ribbons. His screams had reached the house, and I had hastened to the terrible scene in time to hear a whir of wings and see a vague black cloudy thing silhouetted against the rising moon.

My friend was dying when I spoke to him, and he could not answer coherently. All he could do was to whisper, “The amulet﻿—that damned thing﻿—.”

Then he collapsed, an inert mass of mangled flesh.

---

I buried him the next midnight in one of our neglected gardens, and mumbled over his body one of the devilish rituals he had loved in life. And as I pronounced the last daemoniac sentence I heard afar on the moor the faint baying of some gigantic hound. The moon was up, but I dared not look at it. And when I saw on the dim-lighted moor a wide nebulous shadow sweeping from mound to mound, I shut my eyes and threw myself face down upon the ground. When I arose, trembling, I know not how much later, I staggered into the house and made shocking obeisances before the enshrined amulet of green jade.

===Chinese===

此后我们便活在与日俱增的恐怖与着魔里。多半时候我们抱着一个理论：不自然的刺激性生活正合力把我们逼疯；但有时我们更乐意把自己戏剧化成某种悄悄爬行的骇人厄运的牺牲品。古怪的显现如今多得数不胜数。我们孤零零的宅子仿佛被某个恶毒的东西盘踞得活了过来，它本性如何我们无从猜测；每一个夜里，那恶魔似的犬吠都滚过风声呼啸的荒原，愈来愈响，愈来愈响。10月29日，我们在图书室窗下松软的泥土里发现一串脚印，完全无法描摹。它们同成群的大蝙蝠一样叫人无从索解——那些蝙蝠正以前所未有的、与日俱增的数目盘踞着这座古老庄园。

恐怖在11月18日达到顶点：圣约翰入夜后才从阴凄凄的火车站步行回家，被某种可怕的食肉之物攫住，撕成了条条。他的惨叫传到宅子里，我赶向那可怕的现场，恰来得及听见一阵翅膀的呼啸，看见一团朦胧的黑色雾状之物衬着初升的月亮。

我对他说话时，我的朋友已经垂死，答不出连贯的话。他只来得及耳语一句：“护符——那该死的东西——。”

随后他便垮了下去，成了一堆不动弹的、血肉模糊的东西。

第二天午夜，我把他葬在自家一座荒废的园子里，对着他的尸身喃喃念了他生前钟爱的一种魔鬼仪式。而当我念完最后一句魔咒，我听见荒原上远远传来巨犬隐约的吠声。月亮升起来了，可我不敢看它。当我看见昏暗月光下的荒原上有一大片雾状的影子从一个土丘扫向另一个土丘，我闭上眼，脸朝下扑倒在地。不知过了多久，我哆嗦着爬起来，踉跄走回宅中，在供奉绿玉护符的神龛前，行了骇人的跪拜之礼。

===Original===

Being now afraid to live alone in the ancient house on the moor, I departed on the following day for London, taking with me the amulet after destroying by fire and burial the rest of the impious collection in the museum. But after three nights I heard the baying again, and before a week was over felt strange eyes upon me whenever it was dark. One evening as I strolled on Victoria Embankment for some needed air, I saw a black shape obscure one of the reflections of the lamps in the water. A wind, stronger than the night-wind, rushed by, and I knew that what had befallen St. John must soon befall me.

The next day I carefully wrapped the green jade amulet and sailed for Holland. What mercy I might gain by returning the thing to its silent sleeping owner I knew not; but I felt that I must at least try any step conceivably logical. What the hound was, and why it had pursued me, were questions still vague; but I had first heard the baying in that ancient churchyard, and every subsequent event including St. John’s dying whisper had served to connect the curse with the stealing of the amulet. Accordingly I sank into the nethermost abysses of despair when, at an inn in Rotterdam, I discovered that thieves had despoiled me of this sole means of salvation.

The baying was loud that evening, and in the morning I read of a nameless deed in the vilest quarter of the city. The rabble were in terror, for upon an evil tenement had fallen a red death beyond the foulest previous crime of the neighborhood. In a squalid thieves’ den an entire family had been torn to shreds by an unknown thing which left no trace, and those around had heard all night above the usual clamor of drunken voices a faint, deep, insistent note as of a gigantic hound.

---

So at last I stood again in the unwholesome churchyard where a pale winter moon cast hideous shadows, and leafless trees drooped sullenly to meet the withered, frosty grass and cracking slabs, and the ivied church pointed a jeering finger at the unfriendly sky, and the night-wind howled maniacally from over frozen swamps and frigid seas. The baying was very faint now, and it ceased altogether as I approached the ancient grave I had once violated, and frightened away an abnormally large horde of bats which had been hovering curiously around it.

===Chinese===

如今我不敢单独住在荒原上这座古宅里了，次日便动身去伦敦，把护符带在身边，博物馆里其余那批渎神的收藏则付之一炬、掘土掩埋。可是不出三夜，我又听见了犬吠；不到一个星期，天一黑我就觉得有奇怪的眼睛盯着我。一天傍晚，我在维多利亚堤岸上散步透一点必需的空气，看见水中一盏灯的倒影被一团黑影遮暗了。一阵比夜风更疾的风掠过，我知道，落在圣约翰头上的，很快就要落到我头上了。

第二天，我把绿玉护符仔细包好，搭船去了荷兰。把这东西还给它那沉默长眠的主人，能求得什么宽宥，我不知道；但我感到，凡是想得到的合理一步，我至少都得一试。那猎犬是什么，它为什么追猎我，这些问题还恍恍惚惚；但我最初正是在那座古墓园里听见犬吠的，而后来的一切，连同圣约翰临终的耳语，都把这诅咒同盗取护符连在了一起。于是，当我在鹿特丹一家客栈发现小偷已把这唯一的救赎之物从我身上偷走时，我便沉入了绝望的最底层。

那天傍晚犬吠声响得很，第二天早晨，我读到城中最肮脏的街区里一桩无名罪行的报道。那地方的贱民都陷在恐怖里：一幢凶宅遭了洗劫，比这一带此前最污秽的罪行还要骇人。在一个龌龊的贼窝里，一家老小被某种不知名的东西撕成了碎片，那东西没有留下任何痕迹；而周围的人整夜听见，在寻常的醉汉喧闹之上，浮着一种微弱的、低沉的、执拗的音调，像出自一头巨犬。

于是，我终于又站在这座不祥的墓园里：苍白的冬月投下狰狞的影，光秃秃的树阴沉地垂向枯萎的霜草和冻裂的石板，爬满常春藤的教堂向不友好的天空指着一条讥诮的手指，夜风从封冻的沼泽和寒冷的海上癫狂地呼啸而来。此刻犬吠声已极微弱，待我走近我当年亵渎过的那座古坟，惊起一大群反常地围着它好奇盘旋的蝙蝠，吠声便完全止息了。

===Original===

I know not why I went thither unless to pray, or gibber out insane pleas and apologies to the calm white thing that lay within; but, whatever my reason, I attacked the half-frozen sod with a desperation partly mine and partly that of a dominating will outside myself. Excavation was much easier than I expected, though at one point I encountered a queer interruption; when a lean vulture darted down out of the cold sky and pecked frantically at the grave-earth until I killed him with a blow of my spade. Finally I reached the rotting oblong box and removed the damp nitrous cover. This is the last rational act I ever performed.

For crouched within that centuried coffin, embraced by a closepacked nightmare retinue of huge, sinewy, sleeping bats, was the bony thing my friend and I had robbed; not clean and placid as we had seen it then, but covered with caked blood and shreds of alien flesh and hair, and leering sentiently at me with phosphorescent sockets and sharp ensanguined fangs yawning twistedly in mockery of my inevitable doom. And when it gave from those grinning jaws a deep, sardonic bay as of some gigantic hound, and I saw that it held in its gory, filthy claw the lost and fateful amulet of green jade, I merely screamed and ran away idiotically, my screams dissolving into peals of hysterical laughter.

Madness rides the star-wind﻿ ﻿… claws and teeth sharpened on centuries of corpses﻿ ﻿… dripping death astride a bacchanale of bats from night-black ruins of buried temples of Belial.﻿ ﻿… Now, as the baying of that dead, fleshless monstrosity grows louder and louder, and the stealthy whirring and flapping of those accursed web-wings circles closer and closer, I shall seek with my revolver the oblivion which is my only refuge from the unnamed and unnamable.

===Chinese===

我说不清自己为何去那里，除非是为了祈祷，或者向棺中那洁白的静物癫狂地乞怜与谢罪；但无论缘由为何，我抡起铲子掘向半冻的草土，那股狠劲一部分属于我，一部分属于我之外的某种支配性的意志。挖掘比我想的容易得多，只是中途有一处蹊跷的打岔：一只瘦瘪的兀鹫从寒冷的天空俯冲下来，疯了似的啄食坟土，我一铲把它打死。终于，我够着了那具朽烂的长匣，掀开潮湿的硝渍斑斑的盖子。这是我这辈子做的最后一桩有理性的事。

因为蜷在那具百年古棺里的，被一大群紧挤着的、筋腱强健的沉睡巨蝠簇拥着的，正是我与我朋友当年劫掠的那具骸骨；不像我们那时见到的洁净安详，它糊满了凝结的血块和外来的肉与毛发的碎条，用磷光闪闪的眼窝有感地狞睨着我，尖利的、血渍斑斑的獠牙扭曲地大张，嘲弄我那不可避免的厄运。当它从那咧开的颚间发出一声巨犬般的、低沉而讥诮的吠叫，而我又看见它那血淋淋的脏爪里攥着那枚失落的、招祸的绿玉护符，我只是尖叫着，痴痴地逃走，尖叫声溶成一串歇斯底里的狂笑。

疯狂乘着星风驰骋……爪与牙在几个世纪的尸骸上磨得锋利……滴着血的死亡，跨坐在蝙蝠的狂宴上，来自彼列（Belial）那些埋葬神殿的黑夜废墟……如今，那头死了的、无肉的怪物吠得愈来愈响，那些该诅咒的膜翅偷偷摸摸的呼啸与扑打也盘旋得愈来愈近，我要用我的左轮手枪去寻那遗忘——它是我逃离这未名也不可名之之物的唯一庇护。

## The Lurking Fear / 潜伏的恐惧
===Original===



===Chinese===

潜伏的恐惧

## 1 / 1

## 1 /

## 1 / 
===Original===

The Shadow on the Chimney

There was thunder in the air on the night I went to the deserted mansion atop Tempest Mountain to find the lurking fear. I was not alone, for foolhardiness was not then mixed with that love of the grotesque and the terrible which has made my career a series of quests for strange horrors in literature and in life. With me were two faithful and muscular men for whom I had sent when the time came; men long associated with me in my ghastly explorations because of their peculiar fitness.

We had started quietly from the village because of the reporters who still lingered about after the eldritch panic of a month before﻿—the nightmare creeping death. Later, I thought, they might aid me; but I did not want them then. Would to God I had let them share the search, that I might not have had to bear the secret alone so long; to bear it alone for fear the world would call me mad or go mad itself at the demon implications of the thing. Now that I am telling it anyway, lest the brooding make me a maniac, I wish I had never concealed it. For I, and I only, know what manner of fear lurked on that spectral and desolate mountain.

In a small motorcar we covered the miles of primeval forest and hill until the wooded ascent checked it. The country bore an aspect more than usually sinister as we viewed it by night and without the accustomed crowds of investigators, so that we were often tempted to use the acetylene headlights despite the attention it might attract. It was not a wholesome landscape after dark, and I believe I would have noticed its morbidity even had I been ignorant of the terror that stalked there. Of wild creatures there were none﻿—they are wise when death leers close. The ancient lightning-scarred trees seemed unnaturally large and twisted, and the other vegetation unnaturally thick and feverish, while curious mounds and hummocks in the weedy, fulgurite-pitted earth reminded me of snakes and dead men’s skulls swelled to gigantic proportions.

===Chinese===

烟囱上的影子

我去风暴山山顶那座荒宅寻访潜伏的恐惧的那一夜，空中正有雷声。我不是独自去的，因为那时我对怪异与可怖之物的嗜好，还不曾掺进莽撞——正是那种嗜好，使我的一生成了在文学与生活中追索奇异恐怖的一连串远征。随行的有两个忠心的壮汉，是时机到了我打发人请来的；因为体格特别合适，他们早已随我做过多次阴森的探察。

我们是悄悄从村里出发的，因为一个月前那场鬼怪似的恐慌——那场匍匐的死亡的梦魇——过后，记者们还在附近流连。我当时想，往后他们或许帮得上忙；但那时我不要他们。但愿上帝让我带了他们同去，好叫我用不着独自把那秘密扛这么久；独自扛着，只因怕世人骂我疯癫，或怕世人自己在那东西的恶魔含义面前发疯。如今我横下心来讲出来，免得忧思把我逼成狂人，倒宁愿当初从未隐瞒过。因为那鬼魅荒山上潜伏着怎样一种恐惧，只有我，唯独我，知道。

我们乘一辆小汽车驶过数英里的原始森林和丘陵，直到林木掩映的上坡挡住了去路。夜里观看，又没有惯常成群的调查人员，这一带显出比平时更加阴险的面貌，以致我们常忍不住要打开乙炔车头灯，不管它会招来什么注意。入夜之后，这不是一片宜人的风景——即便不知道那出没其间的恐怖，我相信我也照样会觉出它的病态。野兽一只也没有——死神在近旁狞笑时，它们是懂得躲开的。古老的有雷痕的树显得大得出奇、扭得出奇，其余草木也密得出奇、躁得出奇；杂草丛生、满布闪电熔砂坑的地面上，那些古怪的土丘和土墩，叫我想起蛇和死人骷髅涨大到巨人尺寸的模样。

===Original===

Fear had lurked on Tempest Mountain for more than a century. This I learned at once from newspaper accounts of the catastrophe which first brought the region to the world’s notice. The place is a remote, lonely elevation in that part of the Catskills where Dutch civilization once feebly and transiently penetrated, leaving behind as it receded only a few ruined mansions and a degenerate squatter population inhabiting pitiful hamlets on isolated slopes. Normal beings seldom visited the locality till the state police were formed, and even now only infrequent troopers patrol it. The fear, however, is an old tradition throughout the neighboring villages; since it is a prime topic in the simple discourse of the poor mongrels who sometimes leave their valleys to trade handwoven baskets for such primitive necessities as they can not shoot, raise, or make.

The lurking fear dwelt in the shunned and deserted Martense mansion, which crowned the high but gradual eminence whose liability to frequent thunderstorms gave it the name of Tempest Mountain. For over a hundred years the antique, grove-circled stone house had been the subject of stories incredibly wild and monstrously hideous; stories of a silent colossal creeping death which stalked abroad in summer. With whimpering insistence the squatters told tales of a demon which seized lone wayfarers after dark, either carrying them off or leaving them in a frightful state of gnawed dismemberment; while sometimes they whispered of blood-trails toward the distant mansion. Some said the thunder called the lurking fear out of its habitation, while others said the thunder was its voice.

No one outside the backwoods had believed these varying and conflicting stories, with their incoherent, extravagant descriptions of the half-glimpsed fiend; yet not a farmer or villager doubted that the Martense mansion was ghoulishly haunted. Local history forbade such a doubt, although no ghostly evidence was ever found by such investigators as had visited the building after some especially vivid tales of the squatters. Grandmothers told strange myths of the Martense specter; myths concerning the Martense family itself, its queer hereditary dissimilarity of eyes, its long, unnatural annals, and the murder which had cursed it.

===Chinese===

在风暴山上，恐惧已经潜伏了一个多世纪。这一点，我立刻就从最先让这片地方为世人瞩目的那场灾祸的新闻报道里得知了。那地方是卡茨基尔山中一处偏远孤零的高地；荷兰人的文明曾在这里微弱而短暂地渗入，退走时只留下几座倾颓的宅邸，和一群住在孤立山坡上可怜村子里、已经退化的擅居者。正常的人很少到这里来，直到州警成立之后，如今也只有稀疏的骑警偶尔巡逻。然而那恐惧，在周围各村始终是一种古老的传说；因为穷苦的混血乡民有时离开他们的山谷，拿手编的篮子去换那些射不到、种不出、做不出的起码必需品，这恐惧便是他们简朴谈资里的一大题目。

那潜伏的恐惧，栖在人人避而不入、荒废已久的马滕斯宅邸里；宅子坐落在一座高而坡缓的山头上，因为这山头雷暴频繁，得了“风暴山”之名。一百多年来，这座古树环抱的石头老宅一直是种种狂得难以置信、狰狞得骇人听闻的故事的题目：说有一个无声无息的庞然大物爬行的死亡，夏天出外潜行。擅居者们呜咽着、执拗地讲一个恶魔的故事，说它天黑后掳走孤身的行路人，要么带走，要么把他们丢在一副被啃咬过的、肢解零落的惨状里；有时他们还低声说，有血迹一路通向远处那座宅邸。有人说，是雷声把那潜伏的恐惧从巢穴里唤出来；也有人说，雷声就是它的声音。

蛮荒之外没有人信这些五花八门、互相矛盾的传说，连同他们对那惊鸿一瞥的恶魔的语无伦次、天花乱坠的描摹；然而没有一个农人或村民怀疑，马滕斯宅邸闹鬼，闹的是食尸鬼式的鬼。地方志不许人存这样的疑心，尽管在擅居者们讲过什么格外活灵活现的故事之后，也曾有调查人员到那宅子里去，却从未找到一点鬼的证据。老祖母们讲马滕斯幽灵的古怪神话：讲马滕斯家族本身，讲它那遗传的两眼异色，讲它悠久而不自然的编年，讲那桩咒住了全家的谋杀。

===Original===

The terror which brought me to the scene was a sudden and portentous confirmation of the mountaineers’ wildest legends. One summer night, after a thunderstorm of unprecedented violence, the countryside was aroused by a squatter stampede which no mere delusion could create. The pitiful throngs of natives shrieked and whined of the unnamable horror which had descended upon them, and they were not doubted. They had not seen it, but had heard such cries from one of their hamlets that they knew a creeping death had come.

In the morning citizens and state troopers followed the shuddering mountaineers to the place where they said the death had come. Death was indeed there. The ground under one of the squatters’ villages had caved in after a lightning strike, destroying several of the malodorous shanties; but upon this property damage was superimposed an organic devastation which paled it to insignificance. Of a possible seventy-five natives who had inhabited this spot, not one living specimen was visible. The disordered earth was covered with blood and human debris bespeaking too vividly the ravages of demon teeth and talons; yet no visible trail led away from the carnage. That some hideous animal must be the cause, everyone quickly agreed; nor did any tongue now revive the charge that such cryptic deaths formed merely the sordid murders common in decadent communities. That charge was revived only when about twenty-five of the estimated population were found missing from the dead; and even then it was hard to explain the murder of fifty by half that number. But the fact remained that on a summer night a bolt had come out of the heavens and left a dead village whose corpses were horribly mangled, chewed, and clawed.

The excited countryside immediately connected the horror with the haunted Martense mansion, though the localities were over three miles apart. The troopers were more skeptical, including the mansion only casually in their investigations, and dropping it altogether when they found it thoroughly deserted. Country and village people, however, canvassed the place with infinite care; overturning everything in the house, sounding ponds and brooks, beating down bushes, and ransacking the nearby forests. All was in vain; the death that had come had left no trace save destruction itself.

===Chinese===

把我引到现场的这场恐怖，是山民们最狂放的传说一场突如其来的骇人应验。一个夏夜，一场空前猛烈的雷暴过后，乡间被一场擅居者的大奔逃惊动了，那绝不是任何错觉所能造出来的。可怜成群的土人尖叫哭嚎，讲着降临到他们头上的无名恐怖，没有人怀疑他们。他们没有看见它，只是从一个村子里听见了那样的哭喊，便知道爬行的死亡来了。

早晨，市民们和州骑警跟着战抖的山民，去到他们说死亡降临的地方。死亡确实在那里。一道闪电劈过之后，擅居者的一个村子底下的地面塌了下去，毁掉几座恶臭的棚屋；可在这场财产的损失之上，还覆着一层有机的浩劫，把前者衬得不值一提。住在这块地方的大约七十五名土人里，一个活口也看不见。狼藉的泥土上覆满血迹和人的残块，把魔牙魔爪的蹂躏讲得太明白了；然而没有一条看得见的踪迹从这场屠杀引开去。必是某种骇人的野兽干的——人人很快就同意了；这时也没有谁再翻出老话，说这种诡秘的死亡不过是颓败社区里常见的肮脏凶杀。那话头又翻出来，是在估计的人口中约二十五人从死者名册上失踪之后；可即便到那时，要用一半的人数解释五十条人命的凶案，也未免太难。但事实摆在那里：一个夏夜，一道霹雳从天而降，留下一个死亡的村子，尸身个个被狰狞地撕烂、啃过、抓过。

激动的乡民立即把这场恐怖同闹鬼的马滕斯宅邸联系到一起，尽管两处相隔三英里开外。骑警们却较多疑，只把那宅子顺带查了一查，见它彻底荒弃，便索性撂下了。乡下人和村里人却把那地方无限仔细地筛了一遍：把宅子里的东西样样翻倒，把池塘溪流探测了个遍，把灌木丛踩平，把附近的林子搜刮一空。一切徒劳；降临的死亡除了毁灭本身，没有留下一点痕迹。

===Original===

By the second day of the search the affair was fully treated by the newspapers, whose reporters overran Tempest Mountain. They described it in much detail, and with many interviews to elucidate the horror’s history as told by local grandams. I followed the accounts languidly at first, for I am a connoisseur in horrors; but after a week I detected an atmosphere which stirred me oddly, so that on August 5th, 1921, I registered among the reporters who crowded the hotel at Lefferts Corners, nearest village to Tempest Mountain and acknowledged headquarters of the searchers. Three weeks more, and the dispersal of the reporters left me free to begin a terrible exploration based on the minute inquiries and surveying with which I had meanwhile busied myself.

So on this summer night, while distant thunder rumbled, I left a silent motorcar and tramped with two armed companions up the mound-covered reaches of Tempest Mountain, casting the beams of an electric torch on the spectral gray walls that began to appear through the giant oaks ahead. In this morbid night solitude and feeble shifting illumination, the vast boxlike pile displayed obscure hints of terror which day could not uncover; yet I did not hesitate, since I had come with fierce resolution to test an idea. I believed that the thunder called the death-demon out of some fearsome secret place; and be that demon solid entity or vaporous pestilence, I meant to see it.

---

I had thoroughly searched the ruin before, hence knew my plan well; choosing as the seat of my vigil the old room of Jan Martense, whose murder looms so great in the rural legends. I felt subtly that the apartment of this ancient victim was best for my purposes. The chamber, measuring about twenty feet square, contained like the other rooms some rubbish which had once been furniture. It lay on the second story, on the southeast corner of the house, and had an immense east window and narrow south window, both devoid of panes or shutters. Opposite the large window was an enormous Dutch fireplace with scriptural tiles representing the prodigal son, and opposite the narrow window was a spacious bed built into the wall.

===Chinese===

搜查的第二天，这件事已经被报纸大写特写，记者们涌满了风暴山。他们描述得极详尽，还做了许多采访，把当地老妪讲述的恐怖历史一一阐明。起初我只是懒洋洋地追读这些报道，因为在恐怖一道我是行家；可一个星期后，我察觉出一种奇异地撩动我的气氛，于是在1921年8月5日，我也到莱弗茨角挤满记者的旅馆里报了到——那是离风暴山最近的村子，公认的搜寻队大本营。又过三个星期，记者们散去，我可以放开手脚，根据这段时间里我忙着做的细密查访与测绘，开始一场可怕的探察了。

于是在这个夏夜，远方雷声隆隆，我下了悄无声息的汽车，带着两个持枪的同伴，徒步走上风暴山遍布土丘的山坡，把手电的光柱投在开始透过前方巨橡显出的灰色的鬼影似的墙上。在这病态的夜间孤寂和微弱晃动的光里，那庞大的一堆方盒子在白日里藏而不露的恐怖，此刻透出种种晦暗的暗示；可我并不迟疑，因为我是怀着凶狠的决心来验证一个想法的。我相信，是雷声把那死亡恶魔从某个可怕的秘所里召唤出来；无论那恶魔是实体的存在还是雾状的疫瘴，我都要亲眼见到它。

此前我已把这废墟彻底搜过一遍，计划早已想熟；我把守夜的位置选在扬·马滕斯的那间旧屋里——他的谋杀，在乡野传说里赫赫有名。我隐隐觉得，这位古老受害者的房间最合我的用。那间屋子约二十英尺见方，同别的房间一样，堆着些曾是家具的破烂。它在二层，位于宅子的东南角，有一扇巨大的东窗和一扇窄窄的南窗，玻璃和窗板都没有了。大窗对面是一座巨大的荷兰式壁炉，炉壁的瓷砖上画着圣经里浪子回头的图画；窄窗对面是一张嵌在墙里的宽敞的床。

===Original===

As the tree-muffled thunder grew louder, I arranged my plan’s details. First I fastened side by side on the ledge of the large window three rope ladders which I had brought with me. I knew they reached a suitable spot on the grass outside, for I had tested them. Then the three of us dragged from another room a wide four-poster bedstead, crowding it laterally against the window. Having strewn it with fir boughs, all now rested on it with drawn automatics, two relaxing while the third watched. From whatever direction the demon might come, our potential escape was provided. If it came from within the house, we had the window ladders; if from outside, the door and the stairs. We did not think, judging from precedent, that it would pursue us far even at worst.

I watched from midnight to 1 o’clock, when in spite of the sinister house, the unprotected window, and the approaching thunder and lightning, I felt singularly drowsy. I was between my two companions. George Bennett being toward the window and William Tobey toward the fireplace. Bennett was asleep, having apparently felt the same anomalous drowsiness which affected me, so I designated Tobey for the next watch although even he was nodding. It is curious how intently I had been watching that fireplace.

The increasing thunder must have affected my dreams, for in the brief time I slept there came to me apocalyptic visions. Once I partly awaked, probably because the sleeper toward the window had restlessly flung an arm across my chest. I was not sufficiently awake to see whether Tobey was attending to his duties as sentinel, but felt a distinct anxiety on that score. Never before had the presence of evil so poignantly oppressed me. Later I must have dropped asleep again, for it was out of a phantasmal chaos that my mind leaped when the night grew hideous with shrieks beyond anything in my former experience or imagination.

In that shrieking the inmost soul of human fear and agony clawed hopelessly and insanely at the ebony gates of oblivion. I awoke to red madness and the mockery of diabolism, as farther and farther down inconceivable vistas that phobic and crystalline anguish retreated and reverberated. There was no light, but I knew from the empty space at my right that Tobey was gone, God alone knew whither. Across my chest still lay the heavy arm of the sleeper at my left.

===Chinese===

林木闷住的雷声愈来愈响，我把计划的细节一一布置停当。我先在大窗的窗台上并排拴牢三条绳梯——是我随身带来的。我知道它们垂到外面草地上一个合适的位置，因为我试过。随后我们三人从另一间屋里拖来一张宽大的四柱床架，横着挤抵在窗口。铺上冷杉枝后，三个人都持着拔开保险的自动手枪躺在上面，两人歇息，一人守望。无论那恶魔从哪个方向来，我们退身的准备都齐全了。它若从宅子里来，我们有窗边的绳梯；若从外面来，有门和楼梯。而且照先例判断，就算最坏，它也不至于追出多远。

我从午夜守到一点钟，虽然宅子凶险、窗无遮拦、雷电渐近，我却异样地犯起困来。我躺在两个同伴中间，乔治·贝内特靠窗，威廉·托比靠壁炉。贝内特睡着了，显然也染上了折磨我的那种反常的困倦，我便指定托比接岗，尽管他也在打盹。说来奇怪，我竟那样目不转睛地盯着那座壁炉。

愈来愈响的雷声一定侵入了我的梦，因为在我睡着的那一小段时间里，种种启示录式的幻象临到了我。有一回我半醒，大概是因为靠窗睡着的人翻了个身，一条胳膊烦躁地搭上了我的胸口。我醒得不够透，看不清托比有没有尽哨兵的职责，心里却为此悬得慌。从前从没有哪一次，恶的临在这样刺骨地压过我。后来我必定又睡着了，因为当那一夜用我从未经历、从未想象过的尖叫变得狰狞时，我的头脑是从一片幻影般的混沌里猛跳出来的。

那尖叫里，人类恐惧与苦痛的最深的魂，绝望而疯狂地抓挠着遗忘的黑檀之门。我醒来，醒来在红色的疯狂和魔鬼的嘲弄里，随着那阵恐怖的、水晶般的绞痛在不可想象的远景里愈退愈远、回声不绝。没有光，但我从右手边的空缺知道托比不见了，去了哪里，只有上帝知道。搭在我胸口的，还有左边睡着的人那条沉重的手臂。

===Original===

Then came the devastating stroke of lightning which shook the whole mountain, lit the darkest crypts of the hoary grove, and splintered the patriarch of the twisted trees. In the demon flash of a monstrous fireball the sleeper started up suddenly while the glare from beyond the window threw his shadow vividly upon the chimney above the fireplace from which my eyes had never strayed. That I am still alive and sane, is a marvel I can not fathom. I can not fathom it, for the shadow on that chimney was not that of George Bennett or of any other human creature; but a blasphemous abnormality from hell’s nethermost craters; a nameless, shapeless abomination which no mind could fully grasp and no pen even partly describe. In another second I was alone in the accursed mansion, shivering and gibbering. George Bennett and William Tobey had left no trace, not even of a struggle. They were never heard of again.

===Chinese===

随后来了那毁灭性的一记闪电，震动了整座山，照亮了古老树林最黑的深处，劈裂了那些扭歪的树中的老祖宗。在一团巨大火球的恶魔似的一闪里，睡着的人猛然坐起，窗外投来的强光把他的影子活生生地投在壁炉上方的烟囱上——我的眼睛从没有离开过那里。我居然还活着、还清醒，这是我参不透的奇迹。我参不透，因为烟囱上那影子，不是乔治·贝内特的，也不是任何别的人类生灵的；而是一桩出自地狱最深火口的、渎神的畸变；一个无名的、无形的憎物，任何头脑都不能全然把握，任何笔墨都不能描画万一。再一秒钟，我已独自在这受诅咒的宅子里，抖着，语无伦次。乔治·贝内特和威廉·托比没有留下一点痕迹，连挣扎的痕迹也没有。他们从此再无音讯。

===Original===

A Passer in the Storm

For days after that hideous experience in the forest-swathed mansion I lay nervously exhausted in my hotel room at Lefferts Corners. I do not remember exactly how I managed to reach the motorcar, start it, and slip unobserved back to the village; for I retain no distinct impression save of wild-armed titan trees, demoniac mutterings of thunder, and Charonian shadows athwart the low mounds that dotted and streaked the region.

As I shivered and brooded on the casting of that brain-blasting shadow, I knew that I had at last pried out one of earth’s supreme horrors﻿—one of those nameless blights of outer voids whose faint demon scratchings we sometimes hear on the farthest rim of space, yet from which our own finite vision has given us a merciful immunity. The shadow I had seen, I hardly dared to analyze or identify. Something had lain between me and the window that night, but I shuddered whenever I could not cast off the instinct to classify it. If it had only snarled, or bayed, or laughed titteringly﻿—even that would have relieved the abysmal hideousness. But it was so silent. It had rested a heavy arm or foreleg on my chest.﻿ ﻿… Obviously it was organic, or had once been organic.﻿ ﻿… Jan Martense, whose room I had invaded, was buried in the graveyard near the mansion.﻿ ﻿… I must find Bennett and Tobey, if they lived﻿ ﻿… why had it picked them, and left me for the last?﻿ ﻿… Drowsiness is so stifling, and dreams are so horrible.﻿ ﻿…

In a short time I realized that I must tell my story to someone or break down completely. I had already decided not to abandon the quest for the lurking fear, for in my rash ignorance it seemed to me that uncertainty was worse than enlightenment, however terrible the latter might prove to be. Accordingly I revolved in my mind the best course to pursue; whom to select for my confidences, and how to track down the thing which had obliterated two men and cast a nightmare shadow.

===Chinese===

暴风雨中的过客

在那座密林裹住的宅子里经历了骇人的一夜之后，一连几天，我神经衰竭地躺在莱弗茨角旅馆的房间里。我记不清自己是怎样摸到汽车旁、发动它、悄没声地回到村里的；因为除了挥着狂乱枝干的巨树、恶魔般低语的雷声、和横在这满布土丘、丘痕纵横的地域上那冥渡的暗影之外，我不剩任何清晰的印象。

我打着寒噤，反复思量那把脑子炸掉的影子是怎么投下的，我知道自己终于撬出了大地的一桩至高的恐怖之一——那些外层虚空的无名疫瘴之一；它们那恶魔的抓挠声，我们有时会在空间最远的边缘上隐约听见，而我们自己有限的目力，却赐给了我们一种慈悲的免疫。我见过的那影子，我几乎不敢分析，不敢辨认。那夜有什么东西横在我和窗之间，可每当我撵不脱要给它归类的本能，我就发抖。它哪怕只是吼一吼、吠一吠、吃吃笑一笑——那也能解一解这无底的狰狞。可它那样无声。它把一条沉重的手臂，或者前腿，搭在了我的胸口。……它显然是有机的，或者曾经是有机的。……扬·马滕斯，我闯的那间屋子，就葬在宅邸近旁的墓园里。……我必须找到贝内特和托比，如果他们还活着……它为什么先挑中他们，把我留到最后？……困倦这样闷人，梦这样可怕。……

不久我便明白，我得把这事讲给什么人听，否则整个人就会垮掉。我早已决定不放弃对潜伏的恐惧的追索，因为在我莽撞的无知里，不确定比知晓更坏，无论知晓本身可能有多么可怕。于是我在心里盘算最好的行动路线：选谁来托付机密，怎样追查出那个抹掉了两条人命、投下一道梦魇影子的东西。

===Original===

My chief acquaintances at Lefferts Corners had been the affable reporters, of whom several still remained to collect final echoes of the tragedy. It was from these that I determined to choose a colleague, and the more I reflected the more my preference inclined toward one Arthur Munroe, a dark, lean man of about thirty-five, whose education, taste, intelligence, and temperament all seemed to mark him as one not bound to conventional ideas and experiences.

On an afternoon in early September Arthur Munroe listened to my story. I saw from the beginning that he was both interested and sympathetic, and when I had finished he analyzed and discussed the thing with the greatest shrewdness and judgment. His advice, moreover, was eminently practical; for he recommended a postponement of operations at the Martense mansion until we might become fortified with more detailed historical and geographical data. On his initiative we combed the countryside for information regarding the terrible Martense family, and discovered a man who possessed a marvelously illuminating ancestral diary. We also talked at length with such of the mountain mongrels as had not fled from the terror and confusion to remoter slopes, and arranged to precede our culminating task﻿—the exhaustive and definitive examination of the mansion in the light of its detailed history﻿—with an equally exhaustive and definitive examination of spots associated with the various tragedies of squatter legend.

The results of this examination were not at first very enlightening, though our tabulation of them seemed to reveal a fairly significant trend; namely, that the number of reported horrors was by far the greatest in areas either comparatively near the avoided house or connected with it by stretches of the morbidly overnourished forest. There were, it is true, exceptions; indeed, the horror which had caught the world’s ear had happened in a treeless space remote alike from the mansion and from any connecting woods.

===Chinese===

我在莱弗茨角的主要相识，是那几位和气的记者，其中几位还留下来搜集这场惨剧最后的余音。我决意就从他们中间挑一位同僚，而愈想愈属意一个阿瑟·芒罗：三十五岁上下，皮肤黝黑，身形清瘦，他的学养、趣味、智识与性情，处处都标明他是个不受常规观念与经验拘束的人。

9月初的一个下午，阿瑟·芒罗听我讲了这段经历。我从一开始就看出他又关切又同情，我讲完之后，他极其精明、极有见识地剖析和讨论了这件事。他的忠告还极为切实：他建议暂缓在马滕斯宅邸的行动，等我们用更详尽的历史与地理资料把自己武装起来。在他的发起下，我们在乡间到处搜求有关那个可怕的马滕斯家族的情报，找到了一个人，藏着一本照明般明亮的祖传日记。我们还同那些没有在恐怖与混乱中逃往更远山坡的山间混血儿长谈，并安排好，在我们压轴的大事——以详史为光照，对那座宅邸做一次彻底的、决定性的检查——之前，先同样彻底地、决定性地检查一遍与擅居者传说里种种惨案相关的地点。

这番检查起初成效不大，虽然把它们列表归纳后，似乎显出一条颇有分量的趋势：报案最多的恐怖，集中在两类地方——离那座遭人回避的宅子比较近的，或由病态地过肥的森林一段段同它相连的。当然也有例外；的确，震动世界视听的那桩恐怖，就发生在一块空旷无树的地方，离宅子远，离任何连接的林子也远。

===Original===

As to the nature and appearance of the lurking fear, nothing could be gained from the scared and witless shanty-dwellers. In the same breath they called it a snake and a giant, a thunder-devil and a bat, a vulture and a walking tree. We did, however, deem ourselves justified in assuming that it was a living organism highly susceptible to electrical storms; and although certain of the stories suggested wings, we believed that its aversion for open spaces made land locomotion a more probable theory. The only thing really incompatible with the latter view was the rapidity with which the creature must have traveled in order to perform all the deeds attributed to it.

When we came to know the squatters better, we found them curiously likable in many ways. Simple animals they were, gently descending the evolutionary scale because of their unfortunate ancestry and stultifying isolation. They feared outsiders, but slowly grew accustomed to us; finally helping vastly when we beat down all the thickets and tore out all the partitions of the mansion in our search for the lurking fear. When we asked them to help us find Bennett and Tobey they were truly distressed; for they wanted to help us, yet knew that these victims had gone as wholly out of the world as their own missing people. That great numbers of them had actually been killed and removed, just as the wild animals had long been exterminated, we were of course thoroughly convinced; and we waited apprehensively for further tragedies to occur.

By the middle of October we were puzzled by our lack of progress. Owing to the clear nights no demoniac aggressions had taken place, and the completeness of our vain searches of house and country almost drove us to regard the lurking fear as a nonmaterial agency. We feared that the cold weather would come on and halt our explorations, for all agreed that the demon was generally quiet in winter. Thus there was a kind of haste and desperation in our last daylight canvass of the horror-visited hamlet; a hamlet now deserted because of the squatters’ fears.

===Chinese===

至于那潜伏的恐惧的本性与形貌，从吓破了胆、糊里糊涂的棚屋居民那里什么也问不出来。同一口气里，他们把它叫作蛇，叫作巨人，叫作雷魔，叫作蝙蝠，叫作兀鹫，叫作会走的树。不过，我们自觉有理由假定：它是一种对雷暴高度敏感的生物；虽然某些故事提到翅膀，我们相信它对开阔地的嫌恶，使陆地行进成为更可信的理论。同这个看法真正相抵触的只有一点：那生物为了干下记在它名下的全部事迹，行动必须快得惊人。

同擅居者们处熟了，我们发现他们在许多方面出奇地讨人喜欢。他们是简单的动物，只因不幸的血统和闷死人的隔绝，正温和地沿演化之阶下行。他们怕生人，却渐渐同我们处惯了；最后，在我们为搜寻那潜伏的恐惧而踩平所有灌木丛、拆光宅子里所有隔断的时候，他们帮了大忙。我们请他们帮着找贝内特和托比时，他们真是难过；他们想帮，却知道这两名遇难者已经同他们自家失踪的人一样，整个儿出了这个世界。他们中有大批人真的被杀掉、被拖走了，正如野兽早已被斩尽杀绝——这一点我们当然深信不疑；我们提心吊胆，等着新的惨案发生。

到了10月中旬，我们为毫无进展而困惑。夜里晴明，便没有恶魔的侵袭；而宅子内外搜寻的一无所获，几乎逼得我们把那潜伏的恐惧看作非物质的作为了。我们怕天冷下来断了探察，因为大家一致认为，那恶魔冬天大致是安静的。于是，我们对那惨遭恐怖光顾的村子做最后一次白日搜查时，带着一种匆促与孤注一掷；那村子如今因擅居者的恐惧而荒了。

===Original===

The ill-fated squatter hamlet had borne no name, but had long stood in a sheltered though treeless cleft between two elevations called respectively Cone Mountain and Maple Hill. It was closer to Maple Hill than to Cone Mountain, some of the crude abodes indeed being dugouts on the side of the former eminence. Geographically it lay about two miles northwest of the base of Tempest Mountain, and three miles from the oak-girt mansion. Of the distance between the hamlet and the mansion, fully two miles and a quarter on the hamlet’s side was entirely open country; the plain being of fairly level character save for some of the low snakelike mounds, and having as vegetation only grass and scattered weeds. Considering this topography, we had finally concluded that the demon must have come by way of Cone Mountain, a wooded southern prolongation of which ran to within a short distance of the westernmost spur of Tempest Mountain. The upheaval of ground we traced conclusively to a landslide from Maple Hill, a tall lone splintered tree on whose side had been the striking point of the thunderbolt which summoned the fiend.

---

As for the twentieth time or more Arthur Munroe and I went minutely over every inch of the violated village, we were filled with a certain discouragement coupled with vague and novel fears. It was acutely uncanny, even when frightful and uncanny things were common, to encounter so blankly clueless a scene after such overwhelming occurrences; and we moved about beneath the leaden, darkening sky with that tragic directionless zeal which results from a combined sense of futility and necessity of action. Our care was gravely minute; every cottage was again entered, every hillside dugout again searched for bodies, every thorny foot of adjacent slope again scanned for dens and caves, but all without result. And yet, as I have said, vague new fears hovered menacingly over us; as if giant bat-winged gryphons squatted invisibly on the mountaintops and leered with Abaddon-eyes that had looked on transcosmic gulfs.

===Chinese===

那座倒霉的擅居者村子没有名字，久居在两座高地之间一处背风而无树的裂谷里，两座高地，一座叫锥山，一座叫枫树丘。它离枫树丘比离锥山近，有几座简陋的住处干脆就是凿在前者坡面上的地窨子。按方位说，它在风暴山山脚西北约两英里处，离那橡树环抱的宅邸三英里。从村子到宅邸的这段路上，靠村子这头足足两英里又四分之一是全然开阔的原野；平原相当平坦，只有几道蛇形的低土丘，草木也只有青草和星星点点的野草。考虑到这样的地形，我们最后断定那恶魔必是取道锥山而来——锥山一条林木覆盖的南向余脉，延伸到离风暴山最西一条山枝不远的地方。地面的隆起，我们确凿地追溯到枫树丘的一场滑坡；丘上一株又高又孤的劈裂老树，正是那道召来恶魔的霹雳落脚之处。

待到阿瑟·芒罗同我第二十次、或者更多次把这座遭劫的村子一寸寸过完，我们心里已装满某种沮丧，外加崭新的、模糊的恐惧。哪怕在可怖与离奇已是家常便饭的此刻，在这样一场覆天盖地的大祸之后撞见一个如此全无线索的现场，也尖锐地透着邪门；我们在铅色渐暗的天空下走来走去，怀着那种可悲的、没有方向的热忱——它来自徒劳感和行动之必需的合流。我们的细致沉重到近乎苛刻：每座茅屋重新进过，每个山坡地窨重新搜尸，邻近坡地每一荆棘丛生的落脚处重新扫过，找兽穴和山洞，仍是一无所获。然而，如我所说，崭新的模糊恐惧不祥地悬在我们头顶，仿佛巨蝠生翼的鹰头狮隐身蹲在各个山顶上，用看过超宇宙深渊的亚巴顿之眼冷冷睨视。

===Original===

As the afternoon advanced, it became increasingly difficult to see; and we heard the rumble of a thunderstorm gathering over Tempest Mountain. This sound in such a locality naturally stirred us, though less than it would have done at night. As it was, we hoped desperately that the storm would last until well after dark; and with that hope turned from our aimless hillside searching toward the nearest inhabited hamlet to gather a body of squatters as helpers in the investigation. Timid as they were, a few of the younger men were sufficiently inspired by our protective leadership to promise such help.

We had hardly more than turned, however, when there descended such a blinding sheet of torrential rain that shelter became imperative. The extreme, almost nocturnal darkness of the sky caused us to stumble sadly, but guided by the frequent flashes of lightning and by our minute knowledge of the hamlet we soon reached the least porous cabin of the lot; an heterogeneous combination of logs and boards whose still existing door and single tiny window both faced Maple Hill. Barring the door after us against the fury of the wind and rain, we put in place the crude window shutter which our frequent searches had taught us where to find. It was dismal sitting there on rickety boxes in the pitchy darkness, but we smoked pipes and occasionally flashed our pocket lamps about. Now and then we could see the lightning through cracks in the wall; the afternoon was so incredibly dark that each flash was extremely vivid.

The stormy vigil reminded me shudderingly of my ghastly night on Tempest Mountain. My mind turned to that odd question which had kept recurring ever since the nightmare thing had happened; and again I wondered why the demon, approaching the three watchers either from the window or the interior, had begun with the men on each side and left the middle man till the last, when the titan fireball had scared it away. Why had it not taken its victims in natural order, with myself second, from whichever direction it had approached? With what manner of far-reaching tentacles did it prey? Or did it know that I was the leader, and save me for a fate worse than that of my companions?

===Chinese===

午后渐深，天愈来愈难看清；我们听见一场雷暴正在风暴山上空酝酿的隆隆声。在这样的地方，这声音自然令我们震动，虽然比不得夜里。我们只巴望这场暴风雨撑到天黑以后许久；怀着这个念头，我们撇下漫无目的的坡地搜索，转向最近有人住的村子，去聚一批擅居者来帮着查。他们虽然胆小，几个年轻人被我们保护人的架势一鼓动，倒也应承了下来。

可我们刚一转身，便降下一片叫人睁不开眼的瓢泼大雨，躲避成了燃眉之急。天空黑得近乎深夜，我们跌跌撞撞，凭着频频的电光和对村子了如指掌的记忆，很快摸到了其中最不漏雨的一间小屋：一个圆木和木板七拼八凑的东西，残存的门和一扇唯一的小窗都朝着枫树丘。我们进门后抵住风雨，又装上那块粗糙的窗板——屡次的搜查早已教我们知道它放在哪里。在漆黑里坐在摇晃的木箱上实在凄惨，但我们抽着烟斗，不时拧亮手电四下照照。有时能从墙缝里看见闪电；下午黑得出奇，每一闪都亮得逼人。

这场暴风雨里的守夜，使我战抖着想起风暴山上那阴森的一夜。我的心思转到那个自从梦魇般的事发生后就不断回头的问题上；我又纳闷：那恶魔无论从窗口还是从宅内逼近三个守望者，为什么先拿两边的人下手，把中间的人留到最后，直到那团巨火球把它惊走？它为什么不按天然的次序取它的猎物——无论从哪边来，我都是第二个？它用的是怎样的、伸得极远的触手来捕食？还是说，它知道我是领头的，要留我承受一个比同伴们更坏的命运？

===Original===

In the midst of these reflections, as if dramatically arranged to intensify them, there fell near by a terrific bolt of lightning followed by the sound of sliding earth. At the same time the wolfish wind rose to demoniac crescendos of ululation. We were sure that the lone tree on Maple Hill had been struck again, and Munroe rose from his box and went to the tiny window to ascertain the damage. When he took down the shutter the wind and rain howled deafeningly in, so that I could not hear what he said; but I waited while he leaned out and tried to fathom nature’s pandemonium.

Gradually a calming of the wind and dispersal of the unusual darkness told of the storm’s passing. I had hoped it would last into the night to help our quest, but a furtive sunbeam from a knothole behind me removed the likelihood of such a thing. Suggesting to Munroe that we had better get some light even if more showers came, I unbarred and opened the crude door. The ground outside was a singular mass of mud and pools, with fresh heaps of earth from the slight landslide; but I saw nothing to justify the interest which kept my companion silently leaning out the window. Crossing to where he leaned, I touched his shoulder; but he did not move. Then, as I playfully shook him and turned him around, I felt the strangling tendrils of a cancerous horror whose roots reached into illimitable pasts and fathomless abysms of the night that broods beyond time.

For Arthur Munroe was dead. And on what remained of his chewed and gouged head there was no longer a face.

===Chinese===

正想着这些，仿佛有戏剧性的安排要加剧它们似的，近旁落下一道可怕的闪电，随之是泥土滑动的声响。与此同时，狼嚎般的风涨成恶魔似的高嚎。我们断定枫树丘上那棵孤树又遭了雷击，芒罗从箱子上起身，走到小窗前去看灾情。他放下窗板时，风雨震耳欲聋地灌进来，我听不见他说什么；我等着，看他探身出去，试图参透天地的这场大混乱。

风渐渐息了，反常的黑暗渐渐散了，说明暴风雨正在过去。我本巴望它撑进夜里，助我们一臂之力，可身后木板缝里漏进来的一线偷偷的日光，断了这个想头。我对芒罗说，就算再有阵雨，我们也该弄点亮光，说着便开门闩，推开那扇粗陋的门。外面满地是泥泞和水洼，夹着轻度滑坡新堆起的土；可我看不出有什么东西，值得我的同伴一直默默探身窗外。我走到他身边，碰碰他的肩；他没有动。随后，等我半开玩笑地摇了摇他，把他转过来，我摸到了一种癌样恐怖的绞索——它的根须扎进无限的往昔，扎进盘踞在时间之外的那黑夜的无底深渊。

因为阿瑟·芒罗死了。在他那被啃过、被剜过的头颅剩下的部分上，已经没有脸了。

===Original===

What the Red Glare Meant

On the tempest-racked night of November 8th, 1921, with a lantern which cast charnel shadows, I stood digging alone and idiotically in the grave of Jan Martense. I had begun to dig in the afternoon, because a thunderstorm was brewing, and now that it was dark and the storm had burst above the maniacally thick foliage I was glad.

I believe that my mind was partly unhinged by events since August 5th; the demon shadow in the mansion, the general strain and disappointment, and the thing that occurred at the hamlet in an October storm. After that thing I had dug a grave for one whose death I could not understand. I knew that others could not understand either, so let them think Arthur Munroe had wandered away. They searched, but found nothing. The squatters might have understood, but I dared not frighten them more. I myself seemed strangely callous. That shock at the mansion had done something to my brain, and I could think only of the quest for a horror now grown to cataclysmic stature in my imagination; a quest which the fate of Arthur Munroe made me vow to keep silent and solitary.

The scene of my excavations would alone have been enough to unnerve any ordinary man. Baleful primal trees of unholy size, age, and grotesqueness leered above me like the pillars of some hellish Druidic temple; muffling the thunder, hushing the clawing wind, and admitting but little rain. Beyond the scarred trunks in the background, illumined by faint flashes of filtered lightning, rose the damp ivied stones of the deserted mansion, while somewhat nearer was the abandoned Dutch garden whose walks and beds were polluted by a white, fungous, fetid, overnourished vegetation that never saw full daylight. And nearest of all was the graveyard, where deformed trees tossed insane branches as their roots displaced unhallowed slabs and sucked venom from what lay below. Now and then, beneath the brown pall of leaves that rotted and festered in the antediluvian forest darkness, I could trace the sinister outlines of some of these low mounds which characterized the lightning-pierced region.

===Chinese===

红光意味着什么

1921年11月8日，风雨大作之夜，我提着一盏投出藏尸间阴影的提灯，独自在扬·马滕斯的坟里发疯似的挖掘。我下午就动工了，因为一场雷暴正在酝酿；此刻天黑了，暴风雨在疯长的枝叶上头炸开，我反倒高兴。

我相信，自8月5日以来的种种事变——宅中那恶魔的影子，长期的紧张与失望，还有10月暴风雨里村子中发生的那件事——已经把我的心智拧松了半截。那件事之后，我亲手为一个我无法理解其死的人挖了坟。我知道别人也理解不了，就随他们去想阿瑟·芒罗是自己走失的。他们搜寻过，什么也没找着。擅居者们或许能理解，可我不敢再吓他们。我自己倒显得出奇地麻木。宅子里那场惊吓对我的脑子做了点什么，如今我想得到的只有这场追索——那恐怖在我想象里已长到灾变般的个头；而阿瑟·芒罗的下场，叫我发誓把这场追索守成一个人的、沉默的事。

单是我发掘的现场，就足以击垮任何一个寻常人。不圣洁的尺寸、年龄与怪状的凶邪古树，像地狱里德鲁伊神庙的柱子一般在我头顶狞笑；它们闷住雷声，压下抓挠的风，只放进少许雨水。背景里那些带疤的树干之后，借着滤过的微弱电光，耸起荒宅爬满常春藤的湿石墙；稍近些，是废弃的荷兰式花园，它的径与畦都被一种白色的、菌样的、恶臭的、从不见天日的过肥草木糟蹋了。而最近的便是那墓园：畸形的树颠着疯狂的枝桠，根须挤开不圣洁的石板，从底下吮吸毒汁。不时地，在原始森林黑暗里腐熟发酵的褐色叶被下面，我能辨出这一带被霹雳凿穿的地区特有的那些低土丘的不祥轮廓。

===Original===

History had led me to this archaic grave. History, indeed, was all I had after everything else ended in mocking Satanism. I now believed that the lurking fear was no material thing, but a wolf-fanged ghost that rode the midnight lightning. And I believed, because of the masses of local tradition I had unearthed in my search with Arthur Munroe, that the ghost was that of Jan Martense, who died in 1762. That is why I was digging idiotically in his grave.

The Martense mansion was built in 1670 by Gerrit Martense, a wealthy New Amsterdam merchant who disliked the changing order under British rule, and had constructed this magnificent domicile on a remote woodland summit whose untrodden solitude and unusual scenery pleased him. The only substantial disappointment encountered in this site was that which concerned the prevalence of violent thunderstorms in summer. When selecting the hill and building his mansion, Mynheer Martense had laid these frequent natural outbursts to some peculiarity of the year; but in time he perceived that the locality was especially liable to such phenomena. At length, having found these storms injurious to his head, he fitted up a cellar into which he could retreat from their wildest pandemonium.

Of Gerrit Martense’s descendants less is known than of himself; since they were all reared in hatred of the English civilization, and trained to shun such of the colonists as accepted it. Their life was exceedingly secluded, and people declared that their isolation had made them heavy of speech and comprehension. In appearance all were marked by a peculiar inherited dissimilarity of eyes; one generally being blue and the other brown. Their social contacts grew fewer and fewer, till at last they took to intermarrying with the numerous menial class about the estate. Many of the crowded family degenerated, moved across the valley, and merged with the mongrel population which was later to produce the pitiful squatters. The rest had stuck sullenly to their ancestral mansion, becoming more and more clannish and taciturn, yet developing a nervous responsiveness to the frequent thunderstorms.

===Chinese===

是历史把我引到这座古坟前的。历史，的确，是在其余一切统统以嘲弄的撒旦主义收场之后，我仅剩的东西。这时我相信，那潜伏的恐惧不是什么物质的东西，而是一个骑着午夜闪电的、狼牙的幽灵。而我之所以相信这幽灵就是1762年死去的扬·马滕斯，是凭着我在同阿瑟·芒罗一同查访中挖出的成堆地方传说。这就是我发疯似的在他的坟里挖掘的缘故。

马滕斯宅邸是1670年由格里特·马滕斯建造的，一个厌恶英国治下新秩序的新阿姆斯特丹富商；他在一处偏远的林间峰顶造起了这座堂皇的宅邸，那里人迹不至的清寂和不寻常的景色正合他的心意。这处选址唯一实质的失望，是夏季雷暴的频繁。选山建宅的时候，马滕斯老爷把这些频繁的天威发作归之于年成的特别；久而久之他才明白，这地方尤其容易招惹这类现象。最后，发觉这些风暴于他的头有害，他收拾出一间地窖，好从它们最狂乱的大混乱里躲进去。

关于格里特·马滕斯的子孙，世人所知少于他本人；因为他们全在仇视英国文明里长大，受的训练就是躲开接受这文明的殖民者。他们的生活极其隔绝，人们都说，这份隔绝把他们弄得言语与领悟都迟钝了。形貌上，他们都带着一种特别的遗传的两眼异色：通常一只蓝，一只褐。他们的社交愈来愈少，到后来，竟开始同庄园四周人数众多的仆役阶层通婚。这一家拥挤的儿孙有许多退化了，迁过山谷，同后来生出那些可怜擅居者的混血人群汇成一处。其余的固执地守着祖宅，愈来愈抱团、愈来愈寡言，却又对频繁的雷暴生出一种神经质的感应。

===Original===

Most of this information reached the outside world through young Jan Martense, who from some kind of restlessness joined the colonial army when news of the Albany Convention reached Tempest Mountain. He was the first of Gerrit’s descendants to see much of the world; and when he returned in 1760, after six years of campaigning, he was hated as an outsider by his father, uncles, and brothers, in spite of his dissimilar Martense eyes. No longer could he share the peculiarities and prejudices of the Martenses, while the very mountain thunderstorms failed to intoxicate him as they had before. Instead, his surroundings depressed him; and he frequently wrote to a friend in Albany of plans to leave the paternal roof.

In the spring of 1763 Jonathan Gifford, the Albany friend of Jan Martense, became worried by his correspondent’s silence; especially in view of the conditions and quarrels at the Martense mansion. Determined to visit Jan in person, he went into the mountains on horseback. His diary states that he reached Tempest Mountain on September 20th, finding the mansion in great decrepitude. The sullen, odd-eyed Martenses, whose unclean animal aspect shocked him, told him in broken gutturals than Jan was dead. He had, they insisted, been struck by lightning the autumn before, and now lay buried behind the neglected sunken gardens. They showed the visitor the grave, barren and devoid of markers. Something in the Martenses’ manner gave Gifford a feeling of repulsion and suspicion, and a week later he returned with spade and mattock to explore the sepulchral spot. He found what he expected﻿—a skull crushed cruelly as if by savage blows﻿—so returning to Albany he openly charged the Martenses with the murder of their kinsman.

Legal evidence was lacking, but the story spread rapidly around the countryside; and from that time the Martenses were ostracized by the world. No one would deal with them, and their distant manor was shunned as an accursed place. Somehow they managed to live on independently by the products of their estate, for occasional lights glimpsed from faraway hills attested their continued presence. These lights were seen as late as 1810, but toward the last they became very infrequent.

===Chinese===

这些消息大半是通过年轻的扬·马滕斯传到外面世界的；出于某种不安分，他在奥尔巴尼会议的消息传到风暴山时投了殖民地军。他是格里特的子孙里头一个见过大世面的；1760年，六年征战之后归来，尽管长着一双不相同的马滕斯眼睛，却被他的父亲、叔伯和兄弟们当外人恨。他再也没法分享马滕斯家的怪癖与偏见了，连山里的雷暴也不能像从前那样叫他沉醉。相反，他的环境压得他郁郁不乐；他频频写信给奥尔巴尼的一个朋友，诉说离开父宅的打算。

1763年春，扬·马滕斯那位奥尔巴尼的朋友乔纳森·吉福德，为通信人的沉默起了疑心，尤其想到马滕斯宅邸里的境况和争吵。他决意亲自去看扬，骑马进了山。他的日记里说，他9月20日到达风暴山，发现宅子破败不堪。阴沉的、两眼异色的马滕斯家的人，那不洁的兽相骇住了他，用结结巴巴的喉音告诉他说扬死了。他们咬定，他是头年秋天遭雷击死的，如今就埋在荒废的陷园后面。他们领客人看了那座坟：光秃秃的，没有任何标记。马滕斯家人的某种神气，叫吉福德心里生出反感与疑窦；一个星期后，他带着铲子和鹤嘴锄回来，掘开了那处坟地。他找到了他料想的东西——一颗被残酷砸碎的颅骨，仿佛挨过野蛮的棒击——于是他回到奥尔巴尼，公开控告马滕斯家谋害了他们的亲族。

法律证据是缺乏的，可故事在乡间不胫而走；从那时起，马滕斯一家被世人所摈弃。没人肯同他们打交道，他们那偏远的宅邸被人当作受诅咒的地方避着。他们总算靠着庄园的出产自己过了下去，因为从远处山头偶尔望见的灯火，证明他们还在。这样的灯火迟至1810年还有人见到，只是到最后已非常稀少。

===Original===

Meanwhile there grew up about the mansion and the mountain a body of diabolic legendry. The place was avoided with doubled assiduousness, and invested with every whispered myth tradition could supply. It remained unvisited till 1816, when the continued absence of lights was noticed by the squatters. At that time a party made investigations, finding the house deserted and partly in ruins.

There were no skeletons about, so that departure rather than death was inferred. The clan seemed to have left several years before, and improvised penthouses showed how numerous it had grown prior to its migration. Its cultural level had fallen very low, as proved by decaying furniture and scattered silverware which must have been long abandoned when its owners left. But though the dreaded Martenses were gone, the fear of the haunted house continued; and grew very acute when new and strange stories arose among the mountain decadents. There it stood; deserted, feared, and linked with the vengeful ghost of Jan Martense. There it still stood on the night I dug in Jan Martense’s grave.

---

I have described my protracted digging as idiotic, and such it indeed was in object and method. The coffin of Jan Martense had been soon unearthed﻿—it now held only dust and niter﻿—but in my fury to exhume his ghost I delved irrationally and clumsily down beneath where he had lain. God knows what I expected to find﻿—I only felt that I was digging in the grave of a man whose ghost stalked by night.

It is impossible to say what monstrous depth I had attained when my spade, and soon my feet, broke through the ground beneath. The event, under the circumstances, was tremendous; for in the existence of a subterranean space here, my mad theories had terrible confirmation. My slight fall had extinguished the lantern, but I produced an electric pocket-lamp and viewed the small horizontal tunnel which led away indefinitely in both directions. It was amply large for a man to wriggle through; and though no sane person would have tried it at that time, I forgot danger, reason, and cleanliness in my single-minded fever to unearth the lurking fear. Choosing the direction toward the house, I scrambled recklessly into the narrow burrow; squirming ahead blindly and rapidly, and flashing but seldom the lamp I kept before me.

===Chinese===

与此同时，宅邸和山的周围长出了一整套恶魔的野史。这地方被人加倍勤勉地回避着，被传统里一切窃语的神话装点着。它一直无人造访，直到1816年，擅居者们才注意到灯火久已不见。当时有一队人去查探，发现宅子已荒，半是废墟。

四下没有骸骨，于是人们推断是迁走而非死绝。这一族似乎几年前就离开了，那些临时搭的棚顶说明，迁徙之前他们已繁衍得何等众多。他们的文化水准跌得很低，朽坏的家具和散落的银器可以为证——主人弃宅而去时，这些东西想必早已被抛下。可是，虽然可怕的马滕斯家的人走了，对那凶宅的恐惧还在；当山间的堕落者中间又兴起古怪的新故事时，恐惧变得非常锐利。它立在那里：荒废，可怕，同扬·马滕斯复仇的幽灵连在一起。我在扬·马滕斯的坟里挖掘的那一夜，它还立在那里。

我说过我那番持久的挖掘是发疯，就目标和方法而论，也确是发疯。扬·马滕斯的棺材很快就见了天日——里面如今只有尘土和硝石——可我着了魔，要把他的幽灵挖出来，便不讲道理、不顾章法地朝他躺卧之处底下愈挖愈深。天知道我想找到什么——我只觉得，我是在一个夜里闹鬼的人的坟里挖掘。

我挖到了怎样骇人的深度，没法说了；铲子、随即是我的双脚，突然捅穿了下面的地面。在这样的情形下，这一下非同小可；因为此处果真存在一个地下空间，我那些疯狂的理论便得了可怕的证实。我跌的那一小跤扑灭了提灯，可我摸出一只电筒，照见一条狭小的水平隧道，向两头无限地延伸。它宽绰得够一个人钻过去；虽然当时没有一个神志清醒的人肯试，我却把危险、理性和清洁统统忘掉，一心发热，要掘出那潜伏的恐惧。我选了朝向宅子的方向，不管死活地钻进窄洞，盲目而飞快地向前蠕行，把手里的灯拧亮的时候极少。

===Original===

What language can describe the spectacle of a man lost in infinitely abysmal earth; pawing, twisting, wheezing; scrambling madly through sunken convolutions of immemorial blackness without an idea of time, safety, direction, or definite object? There is something hideous in it, but that is what I did. I did it for so long that life faded to a far memory, and I became one with the moles and grubs of nighted depths. Indeed, it was only by accident that after interminable writhings I jarred my forgotten electric lamp alight, so that it shone eerily along the burrow of caked loam that stretched and curved ahead.

I had been scrambling in this way for some time, so that my battery had burned very low, when the passage suddenly inclined sharply upward, altering my mode of progress. And as I raised my glance it was without preparation that I saw glistening in the distance two demoniac reflections of my expiring lamp; two reflections glowing with a baneful and unmistakable effulgence, and provoking maddeningly nebulous memories. I stopped automatically, though lacking the brain to retreat. The eyes approached, yet of the thing that bore them I could distinguish only a claw. But what a claw! Then far overhead I heard a faint crashing which I recognized. It was the wild thunder of the mountain, raised to hysteric fury. I must have been crawling upward for some time, so that the surface was now quite near. And as the muffled thunder clattered, those eyes still stared with vacuous viciousness.

Thank God I did not then know what it was, else I should have died. But I was saved by the very thunder that had summoned it, for after a hideous wait there burst from the unseen outside sky one of those frequent mountainward bolts whose aftermath I had noticed here and there as gashes of disturbed earth and fulgurites of various sizes. With Cyclopean rage it tore through the soil above that damnable pit, blinding and deafening me, yet not wholly reducing me to a coma.

===Chinese===

有什么语言，能描画一个人失落在无底的大地里、刨着、扭着、喘着、疯狂地爬过太古黑暗的下陷的褶曲、不辨时间、不辨安危、不辨方向、不辨目标的景象？这里面有一种狰狞，可我干的就是这个。我干了那么久，久得生活褪成一段遥远的记忆，我同黑夜深处的鼹鼠和蛆虫成了一类。真的，只是在无数次蠕动之后，一次偶然把我忘掉的电筒磕亮，它才幽幽地照出前面那条结着硬泥的洞道，它伸出去，又拐着弯。

我这样爬了有一阵了，电池已烧得所剩无几，这时通道忽然陡然向上，改变了我的行进方式。我一抬眼，毫无准备地看见远处有两点恶魔似的反光，映着我将熄的灯；两点反光，泛着一种不祥而错认不了的光焰，勾起疯人似的、雾茫茫的记忆。我自动停下，虽然脑子已不够退转。那对眼睛逼近了，可托着它们的那个东西，我只辨得出一只爪子。好一只爪子！随后，高高的头顶上，我听见一阵隐约的轰响，我认得它。那是山里的野雷，涨成了歇斯底里的狂怒。我一定已经向上爬了有一阵了，地面离得很近了。闷雷隆隆滚过时，那对眼睛还在空茫地、恶毒地瞪着。

感谢上帝，我那时不知道它是什么，否则我就死了。可救我的，恰是那把它召来的雷；因为在一阵骇人的干等之后，看不见的外面的天上炸下又一记朝山的霹雳——它们留下的痕迹，我曾在这里那里见过：一道道翻起的土缝，一条条大小不一的闪电熔砂。它以巨石般的狂怒，撕穿那可诅咒的深坑上方的泥土，把我震聋震瞎，却没有全然把我打昏。

===Original===

In the chaos of sliding, shifting earth I clawed and floundered helplessly till the rain on my head steadied me and I saw that I had come to the surface in a familiar spot; a steep unforested place on the southwest slope of the mountain. Recurrent sheet lightnings illumed the tumbled ground and the remains of the curious low hummock which had stretched down from the wooded higher slope, but there was nothing in the chaos to show my place of egress from the lethal catacomb. My brain was as great a chaos as the earth, and as a distant red glare burst on the landscape from the south I hardly realized the horror I had been through.

But when two days later the squatters told me what the red glare meant, I felt more horror than that which the mold-burrow and the claw and eyes had given; more horror because of the overwhelming implications. In a hamlet twenty miles away an orgy of fear had followed the bolt which brought me above ground, and a nameless thing had dropped from an overhanging tree into a weak-roofed cabin. It had done a deed, but the squatters had fired the cabin in frenzy before it could escape. It had been doing that deed at the very moment the earth caved in on the thing with the claw and eyes.

===Chinese===

在滑塌翻涌的泥土的混乱里，我无助地抓挠扑腾，直到落在头上的雨点让我定住神，才看清自己已在一个熟悉的地方出了地面：山的西南坡上一处陡峭的无林之地。一阵阵片状电光照亮狼藉的地面和那道古怪低丘的残迹——它原是从上面林坡上伸下来的——可这片混乱里，看不出我从那致命地下墓窟脱身的出口。我的脑子同大地一样是一片混乱；南方天际爆出一道遥远的红光时，我几乎没有意识到自己经历了怎样的恐怖。

可两天之后，当擅居者们告诉我那红光意味着什么时，我感到的恐怖超过了霉洞、超过了那只爪子和那对眼睛——更恐怖，是因为它的含义压倒一切。在二十英里外的一个村子里，那道把我送上地面的霹雳之后，跟着一场恐惧的狂欢；一个无名的东西从一棵低垂的树上，落进了一间屋顶不牢的小屋。它干了一件事，可擅居者们趁它没逃走，疯狂地放火烧了那间小屋。大地在那带爪和眼的东西头上塌陷下去的那一刻，它正在干那件事。

## 4 / 4
===Original===

The Horror in the Eyes

There can be nothing normal in the mind of one who, knowing what I knew of the horrors of Tempest Mountain, would seek alone for the fear that lurked there. That at least two of the fear’s embodiments were destroyed, formed but a slight guarantee of mental and physical safety in this Acheron of multiform diabolism; yet I continued my quest with even greater zeal as events and revelations became more monstrous.

When, two days after my frightful crawl through that crypt of the eyes and claw, I learned that a thing had malignly hovered twenty miles away at the same instant the eyes were glaring at me, I experienced virtual convulsions of fright. But that fright was so mixed with wonder and alluring grotesqueness that it was almost a pleasant sensation. Sometimes, in the throes of a nightmare when unseen powers whirl one over the roofs of strange dead cities toward the grinning chasm of Nis, it is a relief and even a delight to shriek wildly and throw oneself voluntarily along with the hideous vortex of dream-doom down into whatever bottomless gulf may yawn. And so it was with the waking nightmare of Tempest Mountain; the discovery that two monsters had haunted the spot gave me ultimately a mad craving to plunge into the very earth of the accursed region, and with bare hands dig out the death that leered from every inch of the poisonous soil.

===Chinese===

眼睛里的恐怖

在知道我所知道的风暴山种种恐怖之后，还要独自去寻那里潜伏的恐惧——这样一颗头脑，不可能还是正常的。那恐惧的化身至少已毁掉两个，在这条多形恶魔的冥河里，这不过是精神与人身安全的一点薄薄的担保；可事态与启示愈是骇人，我追索的热情反而愈高。

在我爬过那眼睛与爪子的地窟的可怕两天之后，当我得知就在那对眼睛瞪着我的同一瞬间，有个东西在二十英里外不怀好意地悬着，我简直吓出了痉挛。可那恐惧里掺着惊奇和诱人的怪诞，掺得它几乎成了一种愉快的感受。有时，在梦魇的抽搐里，看不见的力量把你卷过陌生的死城的屋顶，卷向尼斯的狞笑深渊，这时狂叫一声、自愿顺着梦之厄运那可怕的漩涡滚进随便哪一道张开的无底深渊，倒是一种解脱，甚至一种快乐。风暴山的清醒的梦魇也是这样；发现有两个怪物在这地方出没，到头来反而给了我一种疯狂的渴望：一头扎进这受诅咒之地的地里，用赤手空拳，把每一寸毒土里狞笑着的死亡挖出来。

===Original===

As soon as possible I visited the grave of Jan Martense and dug vainly where I had dug before. Some extensive cave-in had obliterated all trace of the underground passage, while the rain had washed so much earth back into the excavation that I could not tell how deeply I had dug that other day. I likewise made a difficult trip to the distant hamlet where the death-creature had been burnt, and was little repaid for my trouble. In the ashes of the fateful cabin I found several bones, but apparently none of the monster’s. The squatters said the thing had had only one victim; but in this I judged them inaccurate, since besides the complete skull of a human being, there was another bony fragment which seemed certainly to have belonged to a human skull at some time. Though the rapid drop of the monster had been seen, no one could say just what the creature was like; those who had glimpsed it called it simply a devil. Examining the great tree where it had lurked, I could discern no distinctive marks. I tried to find some trail into the black forest, but on this occasion could not stand the sight of those morbidly large boles, or of those vast serpentlike roots that twisted so malevolently before they sank into the earth.

My next step was to reexamine with microscopic care the deserted hamlet where death had come most abundantly, and where Arthur Munroe had seen something he never lived to describe. Though my vain previous searches had been exceedingly minute, I now had new data to test; for my horrible grave-crawl convinced me that at least one of the phases of the monstrosity had been an underground creature. This time, on the 14th of November, my quest concerned itself mostly with the slopes of Cone Mountain and Maple Hill where they overlook the unfortunate hamlet, and I gave particular attention to the loose earth of the landslide region on the latter eminence.

===Chinese===

我尽快重访了扬·马滕斯的坟，在从前挖过的地方又白挖了一场。一场大面积的塌方把地下通道的痕迹扫荡干净，雨水又把那么多土冲回坑里，我已说不清那天挖了多深。我又辛苦跑了一趟那个遥远的、死亡生物被烧掉的村子，这一趟几乎得不偿失。在那间招祸小屋的灰烬里，我找到几块骨头，可显然没有一块是那怪物的。擅居者们说，那东西只捞到一个受害者；可我断定他们没数清，因为除了一个完整的人颅骨，还有一块骨片，看去肯定也曾属于某个人颅。那怪物从树上扑下来的一瞬虽然有人看见，却没有人说得清它是个什么模样；瞥见过它的人只管它叫魔鬼。我查看了它潜伏的那棵大树，辨不出任何特别的痕迹。我想在黑森林里找一条踪迹，可这一回，我受不了看那些病态地粗大的树身，受不了那些大蛇似的、在扎进土里前恶意扭绞的树根。

我的下一步，是以显微镜般的细心复查那座死亡来得最厚重的荒村，阿瑟·芒罗在那里见过一样他再没活着描述的东西。虽然从前种种徒劳的搜索已够细密，如今我有了新的数据可检验；因为那趟可怕的坟中爬行使我确信，那怪物至少有一个阶段是地下的生物。这一次，11月14日，我的追索主要集中在俯瞰那倒霉村子的锥山和枫树丘的坡上，我尤其注意后者滑坡地带的浮土。

===Original===

The afternoon of my search brought nothing to light, and dusk came as I stood on Maple Hill looking down at the hamlet and across the valley to Tempest Mountain. There had been a gorgeous sunset, and now the moon came up, nearly full and shedding a silver flood over the plain, the distant mountainside, and the curious low mounds that rose here and there. It was a peaceful Arcadian scene, but knowing what it hid I hated it. I hated the mocking moon, the hypocritical plain, the festering mountain, and those sinister mounds. Everything seemed to me tainted with a loathsome contagion, and inspired by a noxious alliance with distorted hidden powers.

Presently, as I gazed abstractedly at the moonlit panorama, my eye became attracted by something singular in the nature and arrangement of a certain topographical element. Without having any exact knowledge of geology, I had from the first been interested in the odd mounds and hummocks of the region. I had noticed that they were pretty widely distributed around Tempest Mountain, though less numerous on the plain than near the hilltop itself, where prehistoric glaciation had doubtless found feebler opposition to its striking and fantastic caprices. Now, in the light of that low moon which cast long weird shadows, it struck me forcibly that the various points and lines of the mound system had a peculiar relation to the summit of Tempest Mountain. That summit was undeniably a center from which the lines or rows of points radiated indefinitely and irregularly, as if the unwholesome Martense mansion had thrown out visible tentacles of terror. The idea of such tentacles gave me an unexplained thrill, and I stopped to analyze my reason for believing these mounds glacial phenomena.

===Chinese===

我搜查的那个下午一无所获；暮色降临时，我立在枫树丘上，俯瞰那村子，望过山谷，望向风暴山。刚有过一场壮丽的日落，此刻月亮升起来，近乎满月，把一片银辉泼在平原上、远处的山坡上、和星星点点隆起的那些古怪低丘上。这是一幅安宁的阿卡迪亚风光，可我知道它藏着什么，我便恨它。我恨那讥诮的月亮，那伪善的平原，那溃烂的山，那些不祥的土丘。在我看来，一切都沾着可憎的传染，一切都靠同扭曲的隐秘势力的毒盟撑着。

不久，当我出神地凝望这月下的全景时，我的目光被某种地物的性质与排布里的奇特之处吸住了。我并不确切懂地质学，可从一开始，我就对这一带古怪的土丘土墩存着兴趣。我注意到，它们在风暴山四周分布得相当广，只是平原上比山顶附近稀少——在那山顶附近，史前的冰川想必碰到的抵抗较弱，遂得以施展它那惊人和奇幻的怪脾气。此刻，借着那轮投下长长的怪影的低月，我猛然看出：这土丘体系的各个点和线，同风暴山顶峰有一种奇特的关系。那顶峰无可否认地是一个中心，一列列的点、一道道的线由它向四面八方不规则地辐射出去，仿佛那不洁的马滕斯宅邸，向四外抛出了看得见的恐怖的触手。这个触手的念头给了我一阵说不清的战栗；我停下来，分析我凭什么相信这些土丘是冰川现象。

===Original===

The more I analyzed the less I believed, and against my newly opened mind there began to beat grotesque and horrible analogies based on superficial aspects and upon my experience beneath the earth. Before I knew it I was uttering frenzied and disjointed words to myself: “My God!﻿ ﻿… Molehills﻿ ﻿… the damned place must be honeycombed﻿ ﻿… how many﻿ ﻿… that night at the mansion﻿ ﻿… they took Bennett and Tobey first﻿ ﻿… on each side of us.”﻿ ﻿… Then I was digging frantically into the mound which had stretched nearest me; digging desperately, shiveringly, but almost jubilantly; digging and at last shrieking aloud with some unplaced emotion as I came upon a tunnel or burrow just like the one through which I had crawled on that other demoniac night.

After that I recall running, spade in hand; a hideous run across moon-litten, mound-marked meadows and through diseased, precipitous abysses of haunted hillside forest; leaping, screaming, panting, bounding toward the terrible Martense mansion. I recall digging unreasoningly in all parts of the brier-choked cellar; digging to find the core and center of that malignant universe of mounds. And then I recall how I laughed when I stumbled on the passageway; the hole at the base of the old chimney, where the thick weeds grew and cast queer shadows in the light of the lone candle I had happened to have with me. What still remained down in that hell-hive, lurking and waiting for the thunder to arouse it, I did not know. Two had been killed; perhaps that had finished it. But still there remained that burning determination to reach the innermost secret of the fear, which I had once more come to deem definite, material, and organic.

===Chinese===

愈分析，我愈不信；对着我这重新打开的心智，种种古怪而可怖的类比开始擂打起来，它们基于表面的形貌，也基于我在地下的经历。不知不觉间，我已语无伦次地朝自己狂喊：“上帝啊！……鼹鼠丘……这该死的地方准是千疮百孔……有多少……宅子里那一夜……他们先拿了贝内特和托比……就在我们两边。”……随后我发疯似的朝离我最近的那道土丘掘去；不顾死活地掘，抖着掘，却几乎带着狂喜地掘；掘着掘着，我终于高声尖叫起来，带着一种安放不下的情绪——我掘到了一条隧道，一条洞道，同我在另一个恶魔之夜钻过的那条一模一样。

此后我记得的就是奔跑，手里攥着铲子；一场狰狞的奔跑，穿过月照的、土丘点点的草场，穿过闹鬼山坡上病态的、陡直的森林深渊；跳着，喊着，喘着，一路扑向那可怕的马滕斯宅邸。我记得自己在荆棘塞满的地窖里到处乱挖，不讲道理地挖，要找出那个恶毒的土丘宇宙的核与心。随后我记得，当我绊到那条通道时我怎样大笑：那洞口开在老烟囱的根上，厚厚的杂草在那里生长，在我碰巧带在身边的一支孤烛的光里投出怪影。那蜂巢似的地狱里还剩着什么、还潜伏着什么等雷声去唤醒，我不知道。已经除掉了两个；也许这就了结了。可我心里还烧着那个决心：要够到这恐惧最里面的秘密——我如今又一次认定，它是确凿的、物质的、有机的。

===Original===

My indecisive speculation whether to explore the passage alone and immediately with my pocket-light or to try to assemble a band of squatters for the quest was interrupted after a time by a sudden rush of wind from the outside which blew out the candle and left me in stark blackness.
