===Original===

On Wednesday, June 25, 1919, after a proper notification of Carrington Harris which did not include surmises as to what we expected to find, my uncle and I conveyed to the shunned house two camp chairs and a folding camp cot, together with some scientific mechanism of greater weight and intricacy. These we placed in the cellar during the day, screening the windows with paper and planning to return in the evening for our first vigil. We had locked the door from the cellar to the ground floor; and having a key to the outside cellar door, were prepared to leave our expensive and delicate apparatus﻿—which we had obtained secretly and at great cost﻿—as many days as our vigils might be protracted. It was our design to sit up together till very late, and then watch singly till dawn in two-hour stretches, myself first and then my companion; the inactive member resting on the cot.

The natural leadership with which my uncle procured the instruments from the laboratories of Brown University and the Cranston Street Armory, and instinctively assumed direction of our venture, was a marvelous commentary on the potential vitality and resilience of a man of eighty-one. Elihu Whipple had lived according to the hygienic laws he had preached as a physician, and but for what happened later would be here in full vigor today. Only two persons suspected what did happen﻿—Carrington Harris and myself. I had to tell Harris because he owned the house and deserved to know what had gone out of it. Then too, we had spoken to him in advance of our quest; and I felt after my uncle’s going that he would understand and assist me in some vitally necessary public explanations. He turned very pale, but agreed to help me, and decided that it would now be safe to rent the house.

===Chinese===

一九一九年六月二十五日，星期三，正当告知了卡林顿·哈里斯一声——不含我们对可能发现之物的猜测——我和舅公把两把折椅、一张行军床，连同几台更大更精的科学器械，搬进了被回避的房子。我们白天把它们安置在地窖里，用纸遮了窗，打算傍晚回来开始第一夜守候。我们锁上了地窖通往底楼的门；临街地窖门的钥匙在握，准备把我们那批昂贵娇嫩的仪器——悄悄弄来、花了大价钱的——撂下多少天都行，守多久撂多久。我们的方案是一同坐到深夜，然后各人分班独守到天亮，两小时一班，我先，他后；歇班的人上床歇息。

舅公从布朗大学实验室和克兰斯顿街军械库弄来那些仪器的天生的干才，和他对我们这场冒险不自觉地担起的主持，是对一个八十一岁的人潜在生命力与韧性的奇妙注脚。伊利胡·惠普尔照着他行医布道的卫生法则生活；倘若不是后来发生的事，他今天还会硬硬朗朗地在这里。只有两个人疑心后来发生了什么——卡林顿·哈里斯和我。我不得不告诉哈里斯，因为他是房主，有权知道从他的房子里出去了什么。再说，探察之前我们同他打过招呼；舅公走后，我觉得他会理解我，并在我必须作的公开说明上助我一臂。他脸色煞白，但答应帮我，并认定如今再把房子租出去是安全的。

===Original===

To declare that we were not nervous on that rainy night of watching would be an exaggeration both gross and ridiculous. We were not, as I have said, in any sense childishly superstitious, but scientific study and reflection had taught us that the known universe of three dimensions embraces the merest fraction of the whole cosmos of substance and energy. In this case an overwhelming preponderance of evidence from numerous authentic sources pointed to the tenacious existence of certain forces of great power and, so far as the human point of view is concerned, exceptional malignancy. To say that we actually believed in vampires or werewolves would be a carelessly inclusive statement. Rather must it be said that we were not prepared to deny the possibility of certain unfamiliar and unclassified modifications of vital force and attenuated matter; existing very infrequently in three-dimensional space because of its more intimate connection with other spatial units, yet close enough to the boundary of our own to furnish us occasional manifestations which we, for lack of a proper vantage-point, may never hope to understand.

In short, it seemed to my uncle and me that an incontrovertible array of facts pointed to some lingering influence in the shunned house; traceable to one or another of the ill-favored French settlers of two centuries before, and still operative through rare and unknown laws of atomic and electronic motion. That the family of Roulet had possessed an abnormal affinity for outer circles of entity﻿—dark spheres which for normal folk hold only repulsion and terror﻿—their recorded history seemed to prove. Had not, then, the riots of those bygone seventeen-thirties set moving certain kinetic patterns in the morbid brain of one or more of them﻿—notably the sinister Paul Roulet﻿—which obscurely survived the bodies murdered and buried by the mob, and continued to function in some multiple-dimensioned space along the original lines of force determined by a frantic hatred of the encroaching community?

===Chinese===

说我们在那个守夜的雨夜里不紧张，是又粗又可笑的夸张。如前所说，我们绝非幼稚迷信的人；可科学的研习与思索教我们明白：已知的三维宇宙，只包容整个物质与能量宇宙的极小一角。本案里，来自众多可信来源的压倒性的证据，指向某些强大力量的顽固存续——就人类的观点而言，凶恶性还非同一般。说我们真信吸血鬼或狼人，是信口开河的讲法。倒不如说，我们不准备否认某些生力与稀薄之物的陌生变种之可能；它们在三度空间里出现得极稀，因为同别的空间单元联系更密，却离我们这一维的边界近得足以时时显形——只因缺乏一个合适的观察点，我们也许永远无法理解那些显形。

简言之，舅公和我都认为，一系列无可辩驳的事实指向被回避的房子里某种滞留的影响；可以追溯到两个世纪前那伙面目不善的法国移民中的一个或几个，并仍旧循着稀有而未知的原子与电子运动的法则运作。鲁莱一家对存在的外圈——对常人只意味着憎恶与恐怖的那些黑暗球层——怀有异常的亲和，他们的有案可查的家史似乎证明了这一点。那么，往昔一七三〇年代的那几场骚乱，是否在他们某个或某几个人病态的头脑里——尤其阴沉的保罗·鲁莱的头脑里——发动了某些动能的图式；这些图式幽晦地熬过了被暴民杀害、掩埋的躯壳，继续在某个多维的空间里，循着最初那股对进逼的社区疯狂的恨意所定的力的路线，运转不辍？

===Original===

Such a thing was surely not a physical or biochemical impossibility in the light of a newer science which includes the theories of relativity and intra-atomic action. One might easily imagine an alien nucleus of substance or energy, formless or otherwise, kept alive by imperceptible or immaterial subtractions from the life-force or bodily tissue and fluids of other and more palpably living things into which it penetrates and with whose fabric it sometimes completely merges itself. It might be actively hostile, or it might be dictated merely by blind motives of self-preservation. In any case such a monster must of necessity be in our scheme of things an anomaly and an intruder, whose extirpation forms a primary duty with every man not an enemy to the world’s life, health, and sanity.

What baffled us was our utter ignorance of the aspect in which we might encounter the thing. No sane person had ever seen it, and few had ever felt it definitely. It might be pure energy﻿—a form ethereal and outside the realm of substance﻿—or it might be partly material; some unknown and equivocal mass of plasticity, capable of changing at will to nebulous approximations of the solid, liquid, gaseous, or tenuously unparticled states. The anthropomorphic patch of mold on the floor, the form of the yellowish vapor, and the curvature of the tree-roots in some of the old tales, all argued at least a remote and reminiscent connection with the human shape; but how representative or permanent that similarity might be, none could say with any kind of certainty.

---

===Chinese===

鉴于囊括了相对论与原子内部作用之学说的新科学，这样一件事在物理或生物化学上绝非不可能。人尽可以设想一个异质的物质或能量的核，有形也罢无形也罢，靠不易觉察的、非物质的对生力——对别的、更可触知的有生之物的生命力或体液组织——的汲取而存活；它渗入那些活物，有时还同它们的构造完全合为一体。它可以是主动怀敌的，也可以只受盲目的自保动机支配。无论如何，这样一个怪物在我们的万物格局里必是异类和闯入者；扑灭它，是每一个不做世界之生命、健康与神智的仇敌的人的头等义务。

难住我们的是，我们全然不知会以何种形貌撞见那东西。神志清明的人从未见过它，明确感到过它的也没有几个。它可以是纯粹的能——一种空灵的、在物质范畴之外的形态——也可以部分是物质的；某种未知的、两可的可塑体，能随意化作固、液、气或稀薄无粒诸态的雾状近似。地上那片人形的霉斑、黄色蒸气的形状、旧传说里某些树根的弯法，都主张它同人的形体至少有一层遥远而依稀的关联；可这层相似有多大代表性、能维持多久，谁也说不出个准。

---

===Original===

We had devised two weapons to fight it; a large and specially fitted Crookes tube operated by powerful storage batteries and provided with peculiar screens and reflectors, in case it proved intangible and opposable only by vigorously destructive ether radiations, and a pair of military flamethrowers of the sort used in the World War, in case it proved partly material and susceptible of mechanical destruction﻿—for like the superstitious Exeter rustics, we were prepared to burn the thing’s heart out if heart existed to burn. All this aggressive mechanism we set in the cellar in positions carefully arranged with reference to the cot and chairs, and to the spot before the fireplace where the mold had taken strange shapes. That suggestive patch, by the way, was only faintly visible when we placed our furniture and instruments, and when we returned that evening for the actual vigil. For a moment I half doubted that I had ever seen it in the more definitely limned form﻿—but then I thought of the legends.

Our cellar vigil began at ten p.m., daylight saving time, and as it continued we found no promise of pertinent developments. A weak, filtered glow from the rain-harassed streetlamps outside, and a feeble phosphorescence from the detestable fungi within, showed the dripping stone of the walls, from which all traces of whitewash had vanished; the dank, fetid and mildew-tainted hard earth floor with its obscene fungi; the rotting remains of what had been stools, chairs, and tables, and other more shapeless furniture; the heavy planks and massive beams of the ground floor overhead; the decrepit plank door leading to bins and chambers beneath other parts of the house; the crumbling stone staircase with ruined wooden handrail; and the crude and cavernous fireplace of blackened brick where rusted iron fragments revealed the past presence of hooks, andirons, spit, crane, and a door to the Dutch oven﻿—these things, and our austere cot and camp chairs, and the heavy and intricate destructive machinery we had brought.

===Chinese===

我们备下了两样武器对付它：一台大型特制的克鲁克斯管，由强力蓄电池驱动，配有特制的屏和反射镜——万一它无形无质、只有强劲的毁灭性以太辐射能与之相抗；还有两支军用火焰喷射器，世界大战里用的那种——万一它部分有质、经得起机械的摧毁——因为同迷信的埃克塞特乡下人一样，它若有心可烧，我们准备烧穿它的心。这些进攻性的机械，我们统统安置在地窖里，位置对着床和椅子、对着壁炉前那片霉痕显过怪形的地方，细细排定。顺带说，我们摆置家具和仪器时，那片意味深长的霉斑只隐约可见；傍晚回来正式守夜时，也是这样。有一阵我几乎疑心自己见过它那轮廓更分明时的样子——随即我想起了那些传说。

我们的地窖守夜始于晚上十点，夏令时。守着守着，不见任何关目要来的迹象。外面被雨折磨的路灯漏进一丝弱光，屋里可憎的真菌发出微弱的磷光，照出滴水的石墙——石灰浆的痕迹早已褪尽；照出阴湿、恶臭、霉污的硬泥地同地上猥亵的真菌；照出曾是凳子、椅子、桌子和其他更不成形之物的朽残；照出头顶底楼沉重的厚板与巨梁；照出通往房子其他部分底下箱柜洞室的破旧板门；照出石级酥碎、木栏朽坏的楼梯；照出乌黑砖砌的洞穴般的大壁炉，锈蚀的铁件透露着当年挂钩、柴架、烤叉、吊臂和荷兰烤箱门的存在——这一切，连同我们简朴的行军床、折椅，和我们带来的沉重精巧的毁灭机械。

===Original===

We had, as in my own former explorations, left the door to the street unlocked; so that a direct and practical path of escape might lie open in case of manifestations beyond our power to deal with. It was our idea that our continued nocturnal presence would call forth whatever malign entity lurked there; and that being prepared, we could dispose of the thing with one or the other of our provided means as soon as we had recognized and observed it sufficiently. How long it might require to evoke and extinguish the thing, we had no notion. It occurred to us, too, that our venture was far from safe; for in what strength the thing might appear no one could tell. But we deemed the game worth the hazard, and embarked on it alone and unhesitatingly; conscious that the seeking of outside aid would only expose us to ridicule and perhaps defeat our entire purpose. Such was our frame of mind as we talked﻿—far into the night, till my uncle’s growing drowsiness made me remind him to lie down for his two-hour sleep.

Something like fear chilled me as I sat there in the small hours alone﻿—I say alone, for one who sits by a sleeper is indeed alone; perhaps more alone than he can realize. My uncle breathed heavily, his deep inhalations and exhalations accompanied by the rain outside, and punctuated by another nerve-racking sound of distant dripping water within﻿—for the house was repulsively damp even in dry weather, and in this storm positively swamp-like. I studied the loose, antique masonry of the walls in the fungus-light and the feeble rays which stole in from the street through the screened window; and once, when the noisome atmosphere of the place seemed about to sicken me, I opened the door and looked up and down the street, feasting my eyes on familiar sights and my nostrils on wholesome air. Still nothing occurred to reward my watching; and I yawned repeatedly, fatigue getting the better of apprehension.

Then the stirring of my uncle in his sleep attracted my notice. He had turned restlessly on the cot several times during the latter half of the first hour, but now he was breathing with unusual irregularity, occasionally heaving a sigh which held more than a few of the qualities of a choking moan.

===Chinese===

同我从前独自探察时一样，我们让通街的门虚掩着；这样，一旦出现我们应付不了的显形，一条直接的、切实的退路便敞着。我们的想法是：我们持续的夜临，会把潜伏在那里的恶意之物引出来；有备而待，等认够、看够它，就用我们备好的这一件或那一件手段打发它。引出并扑灭这东西需要多久，我们毫无概念。我们也想到，这场冒险远说不上安全；那东西会以多大的力量现身，谁也说不得。可我们认为这猎物值得一赌，便独自上马，毫不迟疑；心里明白，寻求外援只会招来嘲笑，说不定还坏我们全部的企图。我们交谈时的心境便是如此——谈到深夜，直到舅公渐起的困意叫我提醒他躺下睡他那两小时。

凌晨时分我独坐守着，有什么像恐惧的东西凉过我心头——我说独坐，因为坐在酣睡者身旁的人实在是独的；也许比他自己能意识到的还独。舅公呼吸沉重，一吸一呼应和着外面的雨，又被另一种折磨神经的、屋内远处滴水的声响点着标点——这房子即便天旱也潮得可憎，这场风雨里简直成了沼泽。我借着菌光和从街上偷过遮窗纸的微光，端详墙上松散的古砌；有一回，那地方的秽气似乎要叫我作呕，我开了门，朝街上两头望了望，让眼睛饱餐熟悉的景象，让鼻孔饱餐健全的空气。守候仍无所获；我频频打哈欠，疲乏压过了忧惧。

随后，舅公睡梦里的翻动引起了我的注意。头一个钟头的后半段，他已几次不安地在床上翻身；此刻他呼吸得异常地乱，时不时叹出一声，那叹息里呛噎的呻吟的成分未免太多。

===Original===

I turned my electric flashlight on him and found his face averted; so rising and crossing to the other side of the cot, I again flashed the light to see if he seemed in any pain. What I saw unnerved me most surprisingly, considering its relative triviality. It must have been merely the association of any odd circumstance with the sinister nature of our location and mission, for surely the circumstance was not in itself frightful or unnatural. It was merely that my uncle’s facial expression, disturbed no doubt by the strange dreams which our situation prompted, betrayed considerable agitation, and seemed not at all characteristic of him. His habitual expression was one of kindly and well-bred calm, whereas now a variety of emotions seemed struggling within him. I think, on the whole, that it was this *variety* which chiefly disturbed me. My uncle, as he gasped and tossed in increasing perturbation and with eyes that had now started open, seemed not one but many men, and suggested a curious quality of alienage from himself.

---

All at once he commenced to mutter, and I did not like the look of his mouth and teeth as he spoke. The words were at first indistinguishable, and then﻿—with a tremendous start﻿—I recognized something about them which filled me with icy fear till I recalled the breadth of my uncle’s education and the interminable translations he had made from anthropological and antiquarian articles in the *Revue des Deux Mondes*. For the venerable Elihu Whipple was muttering *in French*, and the few phrases I could distinguish seemed connected with the darkest myths he had ever adapted from the famous Paris magazine.

Suddenly a perspiration broke out on the sleeper’s forehead, and he leaped abruptly up, half awake. The jumble of French changed to a cry in English, and the hoarse voice shouted excitedly, “My breath, my breath!” Then the awakening became complete, and with a subsidence of facial expression to the normal state my uncle seized my hand and began to relate a dream whose nucleus of significance I could only surmise with a kind of awe.

===Chinese===

我拿电筒照他，见他脸朝里；便起身绕到床那头，再照，看他是否痛楚。所见叫我失魂落魄得不可思议——其实那情形本身相当琐屑。那必定只是任何古怪同我们此地此行阴森性质的联想在作祟，因为那情形本身实在谈不上可怖或不自然。不过是我舅公的面部表情——想必被处境催出的怪梦搅乱了——显出相当的激动，全然不像他。他惯常的表情是一种和蔼的、教养良好的平静；此刻却有种种情绪在他脸上挣扎。我想，最叫我心里发毛的，多半正是这份「种种」。舅公喘息着、翻腾着，骚乱愈甚，眼睛也已瞪开；他不似一人，倒似许多人，透着一种同他自己疏离的古怪品性。

---

他蓦地开始喃喃，他说话时嘴唇和牙齿的样子我不喜欢。字起初辨不出；随后——我心头猛地一凛——我认出了那语气里的什么东西，一阵冰冷的恐惧贯满我全身，直到想起舅公学问之博、想起他从《两世界评论》人类学与古物学文章里做过的那些没完没了的翻译。因为可敬的伊利胡·惠普尔，正用法语喃喃着；我能辨清的几个短语，似乎同他从那家巴黎名刊改编过的最黑暗的神话连着。

骤然间，睡者额上沁出汗来，猛地半坐而起，半醒。法语的大杂烩变成一声英语的喊叫，嘶哑的嗓子激动地嚷着：「我的气，我的气！」随后他全然醒来，脸上收敛回常态，一把抓住我的手，开始讲一个梦——那梦的核，我只能怀着一种敬畏去揣度。

===Original===

He had, he said, floated off from a very ordinary series of dream-pictures into a scene whose strangeness was related to nothing he had ever read. It was of this world, and yet not of it﻿—a shadowy geometrical confusion in which could be seen elements of familiar things in most unfamiliar and perturbing combinations. There was a suggestion of queerly disordered pictures superimposed one upon another; an arrangement in which the essentials of time as well as of space seemed dissolved and mixed in the most illogical fashion. In this kaleidoscopic vortex of phantasmal images were occasional snapshots, if one might use the term, of singular clearness but unaccountable heterogeneity.

Once my uncle thought he lay in a carelessly dug open pit, with a crowd of angry faces framed by straggling locks and three-cornered hats frowning down on him. Again he seemed to be in the interior of a house﻿—an old house, apparently﻿—but the details and inhabitants were constantly changing, and he could never be certain of the faces or the furniture, or even of the room itself, since doors and windows seemed in just as great a state of flux as the presumably more mobile objects. It was queer﻿—damnably queer﻿—and my uncle spoke almost sheepishly, as if half expecting not to be believed, when he declared that of the strange faces many had unmistakably borne the features of the Harris family. And all the while there was a personal sensation of choking, as if some pervasive presence had spread itself through his body and sought to possess itself of his vital processes.

I shuddered at the thought of those vital processes, worn as they were by eighty-one years of continuous functioning, in conflict with unknown forces of which the youngest and strongest system might well be afraid; but in another moment reflected that dreams are only dreams, and that these uncomfortable visions could be, at most, no more than my uncle’s reaction to the investigations and expectations which had lately filled our minds to the exclusion of all else.

Conversation, also, soon tended to dispel my sense of strangeness; and in time I yielded to my yawns and took my turn at slumber. My uncle seemed now very wakeful, and welcomed his period of watching even though the nightmare had aroused him far ahead of his allotted two hours.

===Chinese===

他说，他先是漂过一串顶平常的梦景，落入一个场景，那场景的怪异，同他读过的任何东西都不沾边。它属于这个世界，又不属于——一片影子似的、几何的混沌，其中可以认出熟悉事物的成分，却凑在最不熟悉、最搅扰人的组合里。仿佛一叠错乱的图画层层相叠；一种时间和空间的要素仿佛都被消解、被搅拌成最不合逻辑的拌法。在这万花筒般回旋的幻影涡流里，间或有几幅「快照」——如果可以用这个词——清晰得出奇，驳杂得无法解释。

有一回，舅公觉得自己躺在一口草草挖开的坑里，一圈愤怒的脸，衬着披散的发和三角帽，朝他皱眉压下来。又有一回，他似乎在一栋房子的内部——一栋老房子，看样子——可细节和住客变幻不休，他永远拿不准那些脸、那些家具，甚至拿不准房间本身，因为门窗同那些想必更易动的物件一样，处在同样剧烈的流变里。怪——怪得该死——舅公说这些时几乎带着赧色，仿佛半料到没人肯信：那些怪脸里，有许多张分明带着哈里斯家的相貌。而自始至终，有一种个人性质的窒息感，仿佛一个无所不在的存在已布满他全身，正设法攫取他的生机运转。

想到那些生机运转——八十一年连续运转的损耗，正同连最年轻最强健的体魄也要害怕的未知之力相搏——我不寒而栗；可转念一想，梦不过是梦，这些不快的幻象至多不过是我舅公对近来临门满脑的调查与期待的回应罢了。

交谈也很快驱散了我的异样感；过了一阵，我向哈欠投降，轮到我睡。舅公此刻倒非常清醒，欣然接了守望的班，尽管那场噩梦提前远不止两小时惊醒了他。

===Original===

Sleep seized me quickly, and I was at once haunted with dreams of the most disturbing kind. I felt, in my visions, a cosmic and abysmal loneness; with hostility surging from all sides upon some prison where I lay confined. I seemed bound and gagged, and taunted by the echoing yells of distant multitudes who thirsted for my blood. My uncle’s face came to me with less pleasant association than in waking hours, and I recall many futile struggles and attempts to scream. It was not a pleasant sleep, and for a second I was not sorry for the echoing shriek which clove through the barriers of dream and flung me to a sharp and startled awakeness in which every actual object before my eyes stood out with more than natural clearness and reality.

===Chinese===

睡意攫住我很快，我立刻被最搅扰人的梦缠上。在幻象里，我感到一种宇宙性的、深渊般的孤绝；敌意从四面八方涌向某一处囚禁我的牢狱。我似乎被捆着堵着嘴，被远方渴望我血的人群的回声嘲骂着。舅公的脸浮现在我眼前，比清醒时少了许多可亲的联想；我记得许多徒劳的挣扎、许多想喊喊不出的尝试。那不是安恬的睡眠；所以当那声回荡的尖叫劈开梦的屏障、把我摔进一个尖锐惊醒的清醒里时——眼前每一件实物都带着超乎自然的清晰与真实凸现出来——我并没有觉得可惜。

### V / 五

### V /

### V / 
===Original===

I had been lying with my face away from my uncle’s chair, so that in this sudden flash of awakening I saw only the door to the street, the window, and the wall and floor and ceiling toward the north of the room, all photographed with morbid vividness on my brain in a light brighter than the glow of the fungi or the rays from the street outside. It was not a strong or even a fairly strong light; certainly not nearly strong enough to read an average book by. But it cast a shadow of myself and the cot on the floor, and had a yellowish, penetrating force that hinted at things more potent than luminosity. This I perceived with unhealthy sharpness despite the fact that two of my other senses were violently assailed. For on my ears rang the reverberations of that shocking scream, while my nostrils revolted at the stench which filled the place. My mind, as alert as my senses, recognized the gravely unusual; and almost automatically I leaped up and turned about to grasp the destructive instruments which we had left trained on the moldy spot before the fireplace. As I turned, I dreaded what I was to see; for the scream had been in my uncle’s voice, and I knew not against what menace I should have to defend him and myself.

===Chinese===

我一直背朝着舅公的椅子躺着，所以这骤然的惊醒一睁眼，我看见的只是通街的门、窗，和房间北面的墙、地面与顶棚；这一切在一种比菌光或街上的来光更亮的光里，病态地鲜明地印在我脑中。那光不强，甚至算不得较强；读一本寻常的书断然不够。可它把我和床的影子投在地板上，又带着一种泛黄的、穿透的力道，暗示着比照明更厉害的东西。我以病态的锐利察觉到这一切，尽管我另外两种感官正遭受着暴烈的攻击。因为耳中还鸣着那声骇人尖叫的回响，鼻端则被满屋的恶臭呛得直翻。我的心同感官一样警醒，认出了那非同小可的异常；几乎不假思索，我跃起身，旋过去抓那些毁灭性的器械——我们已经校准、对准壁炉前发霉处的。转身时我怕极了将看见的东西；因为那尖叫出自舅公的嗓子，而我不知道要护住他和我自己，得面对何等样的威胁。

===Original===

Yet after all, the sight was worse than I had dreaded. There are horrors beyond horrors, and this was one of those nuclei of all dreamable hideousness which the cosmos saves to blast an accursed and unhappy few. Out of the fungus-ridden earth steamed up a vaporous corpse-light, yellow and diseased, which bubbled and lapped to a gigantic height in vague outlines half human and half monstrous, through which I could see the chimney and fireplace beyond. It was all eyes﻿—wolfish and mocking﻿—and the rugose insect-like head dissolved at the top to a thin stream of mist which curled putridly about and finally vanished up the chimney. I say that I saw this thing, but it is only in conscious retrospection that I ever definitely traced its damnable approach to form. At the time, it was to me only a seething, dimly phosphorescent cloud of fungous loathsomeness, enveloping and dissolving to an abhorrent plasticity the one object on which all my attention was focused. That object was my uncle﻿—the venerable Elihu Whipple﻿—who with blackening and decaying features leered and gibbered at me, and reached out dripping claws to rend me in the fury which this horror had brought.

It was a sense of routine which kept me from going mad. I had drilled myself in preparation for the crucial moment, and blind training saved me. Recognizing the bubbling evil as no substance reachable by matter or material chemistry, and therefore ignoring the flamethrower which loomed on my left, I threw on the current of the Crookes tube apparatus, and focused toward that scene of immortal blasphemousness the strongest ether radiations which man’s art can arouse from the spaces and fluids of nature. There was a bluish haze and a frenzied sputtering, and the yellowish phosphorescence grew dimmer to my eyes. But I saw the dimness was only that of contrast, and that the waves from the machine had no effect whatever.

===Chinese===

然而说到底，眼前的景象比我怕的还坏。恐怖之外更有恐怖；这是宇宙存下来专轰一小撮受诅不幸者的、一切可梦之狰狞的核之一。从那真菌盘踞的泥地里，蒸起一柱尸体般的光汽，泛黄，病态，翻涌舔舐到巨人般的高度，轮廓半人半怪，隔着它我还看得见后面的烟囱和壁炉。它通体是眼——狼一般，嘲弄一般——那皱壳的、虫一样的头颅，顶端散作一缕细雾，恶臭地卷绕几下，末了钻进烟囱没了。我说我看见了这东西；可只有在意念的回溯里，我才真描出过它那可憎的成形过程。在当时，它于我只是真菌的可憎聚成的一片沸腾的、幽幽发光的云，裹着我全部注意所系的那个对象，把他溶解成一种令人作呕的可塑体。那对象是我舅公——可敬的伊利胡·惠普尔——他正面貌发黑、溃烂，朝我龇牙咧嘴、语无伦次，伸出滴水的爪子要撕我，满腔都是这恐怖灌进去的狂怒。

是一种操练感使我免于发疯。关键时刻的功课我早练熟了，盲目的训练救了我。我认出那沸腾的邪恶是物质和物质化学够不着的东西，便撇开左首的火焰喷射器，合上克鲁克斯管装置的电流，把人类技艺能从自然的空间与流体里唤起的最强以太辐射，对准那不朽的渎神场面射去。泛起一层青雾，一阵疯狂的噼啪，黄色的磷光在我眼里暗了下去。可我随即看出，那暗不过是对比造成的暗；机器的波对它毫无效用。

===Original===

Then, in the midst of that demoniac spectacle, I saw a fresh horror which brought cries to my lips and sent me fumbling and staggering toward that unlocked door to the quiet street, careless of what abnormal terrors I loosed upon the world, or what thoughts or judgments of men I brought down upon my head. In that dim blend of blue and yellow the form of my uncle had commenced a nauseous liquefaction whose essence eludes all description, and in which there played across his vanishing face such changes of identity as only madness can conceive. He was at once a devil and a multitude, a charnel-house and a pageant. Lit by the mixed and uncertain beams, that gelatinous face assumed a dozen﻿—a score﻿—a hundred﻿—aspects; grinning, as it sank to the ground on a body that melted like tallow, in the caricatured likeness of legions strange and yet not strange.

I saw the features of the Harris line, masculine and feminine, adult and infantile, and other features old and young, coarse and refined, familiar and unfamiliar. For a second there flashed a degraded counterfeit of a miniature of poor mad Rhoby Harris that I had seen in the School of Design museum, and another time I thought I caught the rawboned image of Mercy Dexter as I recalled her from a painting in Carrington Harris’s house. It was frightful beyond conception; toward the last, when a curious blend of servant and baby visages flickered close to the fungous floor where a pool of greenish grease was spreading, it seemed as though the shifting features fought against themselves and strove to form contours like those of my uncle’s kindly face. I like to think that he existed at that moment, and that he tried to bid me farewell. It seems to me I hiccupped a farewell from my own parched throat as I lurched out into the street; a thin stream of grease following me through the door to the rain-drenched sidewalk.

---

===Chinese===

随后，就在那魔鬼的奇观正中，我看见了一重新的恐怖；它把喊叫逼到我唇边，教我跌跌撞撞扑向那扇通往安静街道的、没上锁的门，全不顾我把何等反常的恐怖放出到世上，全不顾人们的物议落到我头上。在那青黄交杂的微光里，我舅公的身形开始了一场令人作呕的液化，其实质无从描画；在他那张消隐的脸上，掠过一幕幕只有疯癫才想得出的变脸。他一时是魔鬼，一时是众生；一时是藏尸所，一时是巡游。在混合不定的光的照射下，那张胶质的脸上现出十来种——二十来种——一百来种——相貌；咧着嘴，随那身体像牛脂一样瘫软下去，勾勒出千军万马似曾相识又不相识的漫画脸。

我看见哈里斯一门的面貌，男的，女的，成人的，孩童的；还有别的面貌，老的少的，粗的细的，熟的生的。有一秒，闪过可怜的疯罗比·哈里斯一张劣质的微缩画像的翻版——那原像我曾在设计学校的博物馆里见过；又有一回，我以为捉住了默西·德克斯特那大骨架的形象，正像我记忆里卡林顿·哈里斯家一幅画像上的她。那真是超乎想象的骇人；到末了，当仆人和婴孩的面相混作一团、在真菌的地面上方闪烁——那里正摊开一汪绿油——那些流转的五官仿佛自相格斗，挣扎着想拗出我舅公那张和蔼面孔的轮廓。我愿意相信，那一刻他是存在的，想同我道别。我记得自己踉跄着夺门而出、冲上街去时，从干渴的喉咙里打出一个嗝似的道别；一缕细细的油跟我流出门，淌到雨里的人行道上。

---

===Original===

The rest is shadowy and monstrous. There was no one in the soaking street, and in all the world there was no one I dared tell. I walked aimlessly south past College Hill and the Athenæum, down Hopkins Street, and over the bridge to the business section where tall buildings seemed to guard me as modern material things guard the world from ancient and unwholesome wonder. Then gray dawn unfolded wetly from the east, silhouetting the archaic hill and its venerable steeples, and beckoning me to the place where my terrible work was still unfinished. And in the end I went, wet, hatless, and dazed in the morning light, and entered that awful door in Benefit Street which I had left ajar, and which still swung cryptically in full sight of the early householders to whom I dared not speak.

The grease was gone, for the moldy floor was porous. And in front of the fireplace was no vestige of the giant doubled-up form traced in niter. I looked at the cot, the chairs, the instruments, my neglected hat, and the yellowed straw hat of my uncle. Dazedness was uppermost, and I could scarcely recall what was dream and what was reality. Then thought trickled back, and I knew that I had witnessed things more horrible than I had dreamed.

Sitting down, I tried to conjecture as nearly as sanity would let me just what had happened, and how I might end the horror, if indeed it had been real. Matter it seemed not to be, nor ether, nor anything else conceivable by mortal mind. What, then, but some exotic *emanation*; some vampirish vapor such as Exeter rustics tell of as lurking over certain churchyards? This I felt was the clue, and again I looked at the floor before the fireplace where the mold and niter had taken strange forms.

In ten minutes my mind was made up, and taking my hat I set out for home, where I bathed, ate, and gave by telephone an order for a pickax, a spade, a military gas-mask, and six carboys of sulfuric acid, all to be delivered the next morning at the cellar door of the shunned house in Benefit Street. After that I tried to sleep; and failing, passed the hours in reading and in the composition of inane verses to counteract my mood.

===Chinese===

往后的事，晦暗而狰狞。淋透的街上空无一人，全世界上没有一个我敢告诉的人。我漫无目的地向南走，过学院山和雅典娜图书馆，下霍普金斯街，过桥进商业区——高楼仿佛护卫着我，像现代的物质之物护卫着世界、挡开古老而不洁的奇迹。随后灰色的黎明从东方湿淋淋展开，衬出古旧的坡和苍老的尖塔，招手唤我回那可怕工作未完的地方。末了我去了：湿着，没戴帽子，晨光里晕晕乎乎，进了贝尼菲特街那扇可怕的门——我离开时虚掩着的门——在早起的住户们众目睽睽之下依旧神秘地晃，而他们，我不敢同谁说话。

那油没了，因为发霉的地是渗的。壁炉前，那具硝痕勾出的蜷缩巨形也没了踪影。我看看行军床、椅子、仪器、我那顶被撇下的帽子，和舅公那顶发黄的草帽。晕眩压倒一切，我几乎分不清哪些是梦、哪些是实。随后思绪点点滴滴回流，我知道自己目击了比梦更可怕的实。

我坐下来，在神智容许的范围里尽量确切地推测发生了什么，以及——倘若它真是实的——我该怎样了结这恐怖。它似乎不是物质，不是以太，也不是凡人头脑可想的任何东西。那么，除了某种异样的「散发」、某种埃克塞特乡下人说潜伏在某些墓地上空的吸血的蒸气，还能是什么？我认定这就是线索，便再看壁炉前的地面——霉和硝在那里显过怪形的地方。

十分钟里我拿定了主意。我戴上帽子回家，洗澡，吃饭，电话订购：一把鹤嘴锄，一把铁锹，一只军防毒面具，六坛硫酸——统统在次日上午送到贝尼菲特街被回避的房子的地窖门口。之后我试图睡觉；睡不着，便读书，写些无谓的打油诗，排遣心绪。

===Original===

At eleven a.m. the next day I commenced digging. It was sunny weather, and I was glad of that. I was still alone, for as much as I feared the unknown horror I sought, there was more fear in the thought of telling anybody. Later I told Harris only through sheer necessity, and because he had heard odd tales from old people which disposed him ever so little toward belief. As I turned up the stinking black earth in front of the fireplace, my spade causing a viscous yellow ichor to ooze from the white fungi which it severed, I trembled at the dubious thoughts of what I might uncover. Some secrets of inner Earth are not good for mankind, and this seemed to me one of them.

My hand shook perceptibly, but still I delved; after a while standing in the large hole I had made. With the deepening of the hole, which was about six feet square, the evil smell increased; and I lost all doubt of my imminent contact with the hellish thing whose emanations had cursed the house for over a century and a half. I wondered what it would look like﻿—what its form and substance would be, and how big it might have waxed through long ages of life-sucking. At length I climbed out of the hole and dispersed the heaped-up dirt, then arranging the great carboys of acid around and near two sides, so that when necessary I might empty them all down the aperture in quick succession. After that I dumped earth only along the other two sides; working more slowly and donning my gas-mask as the smell grew. I was nearly unnerved at my proximity to a nameless thing at the bottom of a pit.

===Chinese===

次日上午十一点，我开挖。天气晴朗，我为此高兴。我依然独自一人：对我要找的未知恐怖固然怕，想到告诉任何人，更怕。后来告诉哈里斯，纯属不得已，而且因为他从老辈人那里听过些怪谈，多少肯信一分。我在壁炉前翻起发臭的黑土，铁锹切断白色的真菌，黏黄的浆液从断口渗出；想到可能揭出什么，揣着疑影直发抖。地球内部的某些秘密于人类无益，而这在我看便是其一。

我的手抖得看得出，可我照挖不误；挖了一阵，已站进自己刨出的大坑里。坑约六英尺见方，越深那恶臭越重；我不再怀疑，自己就要同那件地狱的东西短兵相接——它的散发，已经咒了这房子一个半世纪还多。我纳闷它会是什么模样——形体和质地如何，经年累月吸吮生机，又胀到了多大。末了我爬出坑，把土堆摊开，把几大坛酸沿两边摆好、靠好，以便需要时能接连飞速倒进坑口。随后另两边只倒土；干得更慢，气味渐重，便戴上了防毒面具。挨着一个无名的、在坑底的东西，我神经几乎撑不住。

===Original===

Suddenly my spade struck something softer than earth. I shuddered, and made a motion as if to climb out of the hole, which was now as deep as my neck. Then courage returned, and I scraped away more dirt in the light of the electric torch I had provided. The surface I uncovered was fishy and glassy﻿—a kind of semi-putrid congealed jelly with suggestions of translucency. I scraped further, and saw that it had form. There was a rift where a part of the substance was folded over. The exposed area was huge and roughly cylindrical; like a mammoth soft blue-white stovepipe doubled in two, its largest part some two feet in diameter. Still more I scraped, and then abruptly I leaped out of the hole and away from the filthy thing; frantically unstopping and tilting the heavy carboys, and precipitating their corrosive contents one after another down that charnel gulf and upon the unthinkable abnormality whose titan *elbow* I had seen.

---

The blinding maelstrom of greenish-yellow vapor which surged tempestuously up from that hole as the floods of acid descended, will never leave my memory. All along the hill people tell of the yellow day, when virulent and horrible fumes arose from the factory waste dumped in the Providence River, but I know how mistaken they are as to the source. They tell, too, of the hideous roar which at the same time came from some disordered water-pipe or gas main underground﻿—but again I could correct them if I dared. It was unspeakably shocking, and I do not see how I lived through it. I did faint after emptying the fourth carboy, which I had to handle after the fumes had begun to penetrate my mask; but when I recovered I saw that the hole was emitting no fresh vapors.

The two remaining carboys I emptied down without particular result, and after a time I felt it safe to shovel the earth back into the pit. It was twilight before I was done, but fear had gone out of the place. The dampness was less fetid, and all the strange fungi had withered to a kind of harmless grayish powder which blew ash-like along the floor. One of Earth’s nethermost terrors had perished forever; and if there be a hell, it had received at last the demon soul of an unhallowed thing. And as I patted down the last spadeful of mold, I shed the first of the many tears with which I have paid unaffected tribute to my beloved uncle’s memory.

===Chinese===

蓦地，铁锹碰上了比土软的东西。我一哆嗦，动了动像要爬出坑——坑已深及我的脖颈。随后勇气回来，我借预备好的电筒的光，又刮去一层土。露出的表面带着鱼腥光，玻璃似的——一种半腐的凝冻胶，隐约透光。再刮，看出它有形状。有一道裂口，一部分物质折叠过去。裸露的那一大片，粗看是圆柱形；像一截巨大的、蓝白色的软炉筒，对折起来，最粗处直径约有二英尺。我还在刮，突然一下跳出坑去，逃离那龌龊的东西；发狂似的拔开、扳倒那几只沉坛，把腐蚀的内容一坛接一坛，尽数倾进那藏尸的深渊，泼向那不可想象的畸形——我看见了它的泰坦巨肘。

---

酸洪泻下时，坑里狂涌而起的黄绿色蒸气的旋涡，那片炫目的混乱，我终生不忘。山下一带的人到今天还讲那个「黄天」——毒焰可怕地腾起，都说是工厂废料倒进普罗维登斯河的缘故；可我知道他们把源头搞错了。他们还讲，同时从地下某一根错乱的水管或煤气管里，发出骇人的吼啸——这一点，我若敢，也能更正。那场面骇人听闻；我不明白自己怎么撑过来的。倒完第四坛——那是在毒气开始渗进面罩之后我亲手处理的——我晕了过去；醒来时，看见坑里已不再冒新的蒸气。

剩下两坛，我倒下去没有特别的动静；过了一阵，我觉得可以放心把土回填了。填完已是黄昏，可恐惧已离开了这地方。潮气不那么秽了，古怪的真菌尽数枯萎成一种无害的灰粉，像灰烬一样沿地面飘。大地最深的一重恐怖永远死掉了；倘若有地狱，它总算收到了一件不圣之物的魔魂。我拍实最后一锹霉土时，落下了头一滴泪——此后许多滴里的一滴；我以此向敬爱的舅公的亡灵，致一份不掺假的敬礼。

===Original===

The next spring no more pale grass and strange weeds came up in the shunned house’s terraced garden, and shortly afterward Carrington Harris rented the place. It is still spectral, but its strangeness fascinates me, and I shall find mixed with my relief a queer regret when it is torn down to make way for a tawdry shop or vulgar apartment building. The barren old trees in the yard have begun to bear small, sweet apples, and last year the birds nested in their gnarled boughs.

===Chinese===

第二年春天，被回避的房子那台地园子里，再没有苍白的草和怪草长出来；不久，卡林顿·哈里斯把房子租了出去。它至今带着幽灵气，可它的古怪迷着我；等哪天它被拆掉、给一座俗丽的铺面或庸陋的公寓楼让路时，我的宽慰里想必会掺一缕古怪的怅惘。院子里那些不结果的老树开始结小小的、甜的苹果；去年，鸟在虬结的枝上筑了巢。

## The Silver Key / 银钥匙
===Original===

When Randolph Carter was thirty he lost the key to the gate of dreams. Prior to that time he had made up for the prosiness of life by nightly excursions to strange and ancient cities beyond space, and lovely, unbelievable garden lands across ethereal seas; but as middle age hardened upon him he felt these liberties slipping away little by little, until at last he was cut off altogether. No more could his galleys sail up the river Oukranos past the gilded spires of Thran, or his elephant caravans tramp through perfumed jungles in Kled, where forgotten palaces with veined ivory columns sleep lovely and unbroken under the moon.

He had read too much of things as they are, and talked with too many people. Well-meaning philosophers had taught him to look into the logical relations of things, and analyze the processes which shaped his thoughts and fancies. Wonder had gone away, and he had forgotten that all life is only a set of pictures in the brain, among which there is no difference betwixt those born of real things and those born of inward dreamings, and no cause to value the one above the other. Custom had dinned into his ears a superstitious reverence for that which tangibly and physically exists, and had made him secretly ashamed to dwell in visions. Wise men told him his simple fancies were inane and childish, and he believed it because he could see that they might easily be so. What he failed to recall was that the deeds of reality are just as inane and childish, and even more absurd because their actors persist in fancying them full of meaning and purpose as the blind purpose grinds aimlessly on from nothing to something back to nothing again, neither heeding nor knowing the wishes or existence of the minds that flicker for a second now and then in the darkness.

===Chinese===

兰道夫·卡特三十岁那年，弄丢了通往梦境之门的那把钥匙。在那之前，他一直靠夜夜远足来补偿生活的平淡——到空间之外陌生古老的城市，到以太之海彼岸可爱得叫人不敢相信的花园国度；可中年一上身，他感到这些特权一点点溜走，直到最后被整个切断。他的桨帆船再不能溯乌克拉诺斯河而上，驶过特兰的镀金尖塔；他的象队再不能踏过克莱德的香丛林，那里被遗忘的宫殿，带纹理的象牙柱，在月下完好而可爱地长眠。

他把「实然」读得太多，同太多人谈过话。好心的哲学家教他去看事物之间的逻辑关系，去分析塑造他思想与幻想的过程。奇迹走掉了；他忘掉了：全部生命不过是脑中的一组图像，其中生于实物的同生于内在之梦的，毫无分别，也没有理由高此低彼。习惯朝他耳朵里灌输了对于有形有质之物的迷信敬意，使他暗自以栖身幻象为耻。智者们告诉他，他那点朴素的幻想空洞而幼稚，他信了，因为他看得出它们确实容易如此。他没能记起的是：现实的行为同样空洞而幼稚，而且更加荒唐，因为演戏的人偏执意以为它们充满意义和目的——当那盲目的目的漫无目标地从无到有、再从有到无地碾磨，对不时在黑暗里闪亮一秒的那些心智的愿望或存在，既不留心，也无所知。

===Original===

They had chained him down to things that are, and had then explained the workings of those things till mystery had gone out of the world. When he complained, and longed to escape into twilight realms where magic molded all the little vivid fragments and prized associations of his mind into vistas of breathless expectancy and unquenchable delight, they turned him instead toward the newfound prodigies of science, bidding him find wonder in the atom’s vortex and mystery in the sky’s dimensions. And when he had failed to find these boons in things whose laws are known and measurable, they told him he lacked imagination, and was immature because he preferred dream-illusions to the illusions of our physical creation.

So Carter had tried to do as others did, and pretended that the common events and emotions of earthly minds were more important than the fantasies of rare and delicate souls. He did not dissent when they told him that the animal pain of a stuck pig or dyspeptic plowman in real life is a greater thing than the peerless beauty of Narath with its hundred carven gates and domes of chalcedony, which he dimly remembered from his dreams; and under their guidance he cultivated a painstaking sense of pity and tragedy.

Once in a while, though, he could not help seeing how shallow, fickle, and meaningless all human aspirations are, and how emptily our real impulses contrast with those pompous ideals we profess to hold. Then he would have recourse to the polite laughter they had taught him to use against the extravagance and artificiality of dreams; for he saw that the daily life of our world is every inch as extravagant and artificial, and far less worthy of respect because of its poverty in beauty and its silly reluctance to admit its own lack of reason and purpose. In this way he became a kind of humorist, for he did not see that even humor is empty in a mindless universe devoid of any true standard of consistency or inconsistency.

===Chinese===

他们把他锁链在「实然」之物上，然后讲解这些东西的机理，直到神秘离开世界。当他抱怨、渴望逃进暮色的国度——在那里，魔法把他心里一切鲜活的小碎片和珍视的联想，捏合成令人屏息的期待和不灭的喜悦——他们却把他拨向科学的新奇迹，吩咐他在原子的涡旋里找奇迹，在天穹的维度里找神秘。而当他在这些定律已知可测的东西里找不到这些恩惠，他们便说他缺乏想象力，说他不成熟，因为他宁要梦的幻象，不要我们这个物质造物的幻象。

于是卡特学着像旁人那样行事，假装尘世心智的寻常事件和情感，比稀有而精微的灵魂的幻想更重要。他们对他说，现实中一头被刺的猪或一个消化不良的农夫的畜生之痛，比纳拉斯无与伦比的美更重要——那百座雕门和玉髓穹顶的纳拉斯，他还在梦里依稀记得——他不表异议；在他们的引导下，他培养起一种勤恳的悲悯与悲剧感。

不过偶尔，他仍不免看出人类的一切抱负多么浅薄、善变、无谓；我们真实的冲动同我们公然标榜的那些堂皇理想对照，何其空洞。这时他便动用他们教他的那种文雅的嘲笑，去笑梦的铺张和做作；因为他看到，我们世界的日常生活一样铺张、一样做作，而且更不值得尊重——既贫于美，又愚蠢地不肯承认自己没有理性与目的。就这样他成了某种幽默家；他没有看到，在一个没有心智的宇宙里，在一个没有任何真章法可讲「一致」与「不一致」的宇宙里，连幽默也是空的。

===Original===

In the first days of his bondage he had turned to the gentle churchly faith endeared to him by the naive trust of his fathers, for thence stretched mystic avenues which seemed to promise escape from life. Only on closer view did he mark the starved fancy and beauty, the stale and prosy triteness, and the owlish gravity and grotesque claims of solid truth which reigned boresomely and overwhelmingly among most of its professors; or feel to the full the awkwardness with which it sought to keep alive as literal fact the outgrown fears and guesses of a primal race confronting the unknown. It wearied Carter to see how solemnly people tried to make earthly reality out of old myths which every step of their boasted science confuted, and this misplaced seriousness killed the attachment he might have kept for the ancient creeds had they been content to offer the sonorous rites and emotional outlets in their true guise of ethereal fantasy.

But when he came to study those who had thrown off the old myths, he found them even more ugly than those who had not. They did not know that beauty lies in harmony, and that loveliness of life has no standard amidst an aimless cosmos save only its harmony with the dreams and the feelings which have gone before and blindly molded our little spheres out of the rest of chaos. They did not see that good and evil and beauty and ugliness are only ornamental fruits of perspective, whose sole value lies in their linkage to what chance made our fathers think and feel, and whose fine details are different for every race and culture. Instead, they either denied these things altogether or transferred them to the crude, vague instincts which they shared with the beasts and peasants; so that their lives were dragged malodorously out in pain, ugliness, and disproportion, yet filled with a ludicrous pride at having escaped from something no more unsound than that which still held them. They had traded the false gods of fear and blind piety for those of license and anarchy.

===Chinese===

在受缚的最初日子里，他曾转向慈和的教会信仰——先人天真的信托使它在他心里可亲，因为从那里伸出神秘的长街，仿佛许诺着对生活的逃离。只是细看之下，他才看清其中挨饿的幻想与美、陈腐平淡的滥调，看清猫头鹰式的凝重和「坚实真理」的怪样主张，在多数信奉者中间无聊而压倒一切地统治着；也才充分感到，它何等笨拙地想把一个原始种族面对未知时的过时的恐惧与猜测，当作字面事实养活下去。人们那么郑重其事地想把古老神话做成地上的实在，而他们引以为豪的科学的每一步都在拆它的台；这错置的严肃，杀死了他本可能为古老信条保有的依恋——倘若那些信条安于以空灵幻想的本来面目，献上铿锵的祭仪和情感的出口。

可等他来研究那些抛掉了旧神话的人，他发现他们比没抛掉的更丑。他们不知道美在于和谐；不知道生命之可爱，在一个漫无目的的宇宙里没有别的标准，只有同先前的梦与情感的和谐——正是那些梦与情感，盲目地把我们的小小圆球从其余的混沌里捏了出来。他们看不到，善与恶、美与丑，不过是视角的装饰果，其全部价值只在于它们同偶然令我们先人所思所感的关联，其精微的细节，各个种族与文化各不相同。他们非此即彼：或者干脆否认这些东西，或者把它们转交给同野兽和农夫共享的粗糙含混的本能；于是他们的生命在疼痛、丑陋和失称里臭烘烘地拖长，却怀着一种可笑的骄傲，自庆逃脱了什么——那东西未必比仍旧攥着他们的更站不住。他们用放纵与无序的新神，换掉了恐惧与盲目虔诚的旧神。

===Original===

Carter did not taste deeply of these modern freedoms; for their cheapness and squalor sickened a spirit loving beauty alone, while his reason rebelled at the flimsy logic with which their champions tried to gild brute impulse with a sacredness stripped from the idols they had discarded. He saw that most of them, in common with their cast-off priestcraft, could not escape from the delusion that life has a meaning apart from that which men dream into it; and could not lay aside the crude notion of ethics and obligations beyond those of beauty, even when all Nature shrieked of its unconsciousness and impersonal unmorality in the light of their scientific discoveries. Warped and bigoted with preconceived illusions of justice, freedom, and consistency, they cast off the old lore and the old ways with the old beliefs; nor ever stopped to think that that lore and those ways were the sole makers of their present thoughts and judgments, and the sole guides and standards in a meaningless universe without fixed aims or stable points of reference. Having lost these artificial settings, their lives grew void of direction and dramatic interest; till at length they strove to drown their ennui in bustle and pretended usefulness, noise and excitement, barbaric display and animal sensation. When these things palled, disappointed, or grew nauseous through revulsion, they cultivated irony and bitterness, and found fault with the social order. Never could they realize that their brute foundations were as shifting and contradictory as the gods of their elders, and that the satisfaction of one moment is the bane of the next. Calm, lasting beauty comes only in dream, and this solace the world had thrown away when in its worship of the real it threw away the secrets of childhood and innocence.

===Chinese===

这些现代的自由，卡特没有深尝；它们的廉价和鄙陋叫一个只爱美的灵魂作呕，而它们的鼓吹者拿从丢弃的神像上剥下来的神圣，去给畜生的冲动镀金，那逻辑的单薄，也叫他的理性不服。他看出，他们同他们抛掉的僧侣阶层一样，逃不出一种错觉：以为生命有某种意义，独立于人们梦进生命里的那一种；放不下伦理与义务的粗糙观念——超越于美之义务的观念——哪怕他们自己的科学发现已在光天化日下大声喊出自然无心无己、无善无恶。被先入为主的正义、自由与一致的幻象扭坏了、闭死了，他们连同旧信仰一起抛掉了旧学和旧俗；却从不曾停下来想一想：那学问和那些习俗，是他们当下思想与判断的唯一制造者，是在一个没有固定目标、没有稳定参照点的宇宙里仅有的向导和标准。失了这些人为的凭依，他们的生命便没了方向和戏剧的兴趣；到末了，只好在忙碌和假充有用里、在喧嚣和刺激里、在蛮荒的排场和畜生的感官里，淹死他们的无聊。这些东西腻了、败兴了、或因反胃而可憎了，他们就培养讥诮和刻毒，指摘社会秩序。他们永远不能明白：他们那畜生的地基同他们长辈的神一样摇摆而自相矛盾；此刻的满足正是下一刻的祸根。宁静而持久的美只在梦里；这慰藉，世界在崇拜实在、抛掉童年与天真的秘密时，已经一并抛掉了。

===Original===

Amidst this chaos of hollowness and unrest Carter tried to live as befitted a man of keen thought and good heritage. With his dreams fading under the ridicule of the age he could not believe in anything, but the love of harmony kept him close to the ways of his race and station. He walked impassive through the cities of men, and sighed because no vista seemed fully real; because every flash of yellow sunlight on tall roofs and every glimpse of balustraded plazas in the first lamps of evening served only to remind him of dreams he had once known, and to make him homesick for ethereal lands he no longer knew how to find. Travel was only a mockery; and even the Great War stirred him but little, though he served from the first in the Foreign Legion of France. For a while he sought friends, but soon grew weary of the crudeness of their emotions, and the sameness and earthiness of their visions. He felt vaguely glad that all his relatives were distant and out of touch with him, for they could not have understood his mental life. That is, none but his grandfather and great-uncle Christopher could, and they were long dead.

Then he began once more the writing of books, which he had left off when dreams first failed him. But here, too, was there no satisfaction or fulfilment; for the touch of earth was upon his mind, and he could not think of lovely things as he had done of yore. Ironic humor dragged down all the twilight minarets he reared, and the earthy fear of improbability blasted all the delicate and amazing flowers in his faery gardens. The convention of assumed piety spilt mawkishness on his characters, while the myth of an important reality and significant human events and emotions debased all his high fantasy into thin-veiled allegory and cheap social satire. His new novels were successful as his old ones had never been; and because he knew how empty they must be to please an empty herd, he burned them and ceased his writing. They were very graceful novels, in which he urbanely laughed at the dreams he lightly sketched; but he saw that their sophistication had sapped all their life away.

---

===Chinese===

在这空洞与不安的混沌中，卡特尽量像一个思想敏锐、家世良好的人那样生活。梦在时代的讪笑下褪色，他什么也不能信；但对和谐的爱使他守着本阶层本门第的道路。他漠然走过人群的城市，叹息没有一片风景显得全然真实；因为高楼上一抹斜阳、傍晚初灯里栏杆广场的一瞥，都只叫他想起重曾知道的梦，叫他怀恋以太的土地——他已不知怎样再找到的地方。旅行只是嘲弄；连大战也只淡淡地动他一动，尽管他从头到尾在法国外籍军团服役。有一阵他寻朋友，但很快就腻了他们情感的粗糙、他们眼界的人间气和一律。他隐隐庆幸亲戚们都疏远而不通音讯，因为他们无法理解他的精神生活。也就是说，除了祖父和伯公克里斯托弗，而他们早已不在人世。

随后他重新开始写书——梦初次背弃他时撂下的。可这里也没有满足与圆成；因为尘世的触角已搭上他的头脑，他再不能像旧日那样想可爱的事物了。讥诮的幽默拖倒了他竖起的暮色尖塔；对「不可能」的人间恐惧，轰毁了他仙乡花园里一切精巧惊人的花。假充虔诚的惯例把甜腻泼上他的人物；「实在重要」的神话——重要的人类事件与情感——又把他全部的高幻想贬成薄纱的寓言和廉价的社会讽刺。他的新小说成功了，旧作从未这样成功过；正因为他知道它们必定空洞，才能取悦空洞的一群，他把它们烧了，辍笔不写。那些小说风雅得很，他在里面文雅地笑他自己轻轻勾勒的梦；可他看出，那份世故把小说的生命淘空了。

---

===Original===

It was after this that he cultivated deliberate illusion, and dabbled in the notions of the bizarre and the eccentric as an antidote for the commonplace. Most of these, however, soon showed their poverty and barrenness; and he saw that the popular doctrines of occultism are as dry and inflexible as those of science, yet without even the slender palliative of truth to redeem them. Gross stupidity, falsehood, and muddled thinking are not dream; and form no escape from life to a mind trained above their level. So Carter bought stranger books and sought out deeper and more terrible men of fantastic erudition; delving into arcana of consciousness that few have trod, and learning things about the secret pits of life, legend, and immemorial antiquity which disturbed him ever afterward. He decided to live on a rarer plane, and furnished his Boston home to suit his changing moods; one room for each, hung in appropriate colors, furnished with befitting books and objects, and provided with sources of the proper sensations of light, heat, sound, taste, and odor.

Once he heard of a man in the South who was shunned and feared for the blasphemous things he read in prehistoric books and clay tablets smuggled from India and Arabia. Him he visited, living with him and sharing his studies for seven years, till horror overtook them one midnight in an unknown and archaic graveyard, and only one emerged where two had entered. Then he went back to Arkham, the terrible witch-haunted old town of his forefathers in New England, and had experiences in the dark, amidst the hoary willows and tottering gambrel roofs, which made him seal forever certain pages in the diary of a wild-minded ancestor. But these horrors took him only to the edge of reality, and were not of the true dream country he had known in youth; so that at fifty he despaired of any rest or contentment in a world grown too busy for beauty and too shrewd for dream.

===Chinese===

在此之后，他培养起蓄意的幻境，把怪异和偏执的念头当寻常生活的解毒剂来沾。可这些东西多半很快显出贫瘠和荒凉；他看出流行的秘术教条同科学的教条一样干硬僵死，还没有真理那点细瘦的止痛膏来救赎。粗劣的愚蠢、谎言和浆糊头脑不是梦；对一个水准在其上的头脑，构不成对生活的逃离。于是卡特买更怪的书，寻更深更怕人的奇学之士；探入少有人迹的意识秘境，学到关于生命、传说和太古的秘密深坑的种种——此后一直搅扰着他。他决意活在一个更稀薄的层面上，把他波士顿的住宅按他流转的心境布置；一个心境一间屋，挂相应的颜色，配相应的书与物，设相应的光、热、声、味、气的正当来源。

有一回他听说南方有个人，因读史前书籍和从印度阿拉伯走私来的泥板上的渎神之物而遭人畏避。他去拜访了他，同他一起生活、一起研究了七年，直到恐怖在一个午夜赶上他们——在一座无名的古墓地里，进去两人，出来一人。随后他回了阿卡姆，新英格兰他祖上那座闹巫的可怕老城，在苍老的柳树和倾颓的复斜屋顶间、在黑暗里经了些事，叫他永远封死了一位狂放先人日记里的某几页。可这些恐怖只把他带到实在的边缘，不属于他青年时代知道的真梦乡；于是到了五十岁，他对这个世界——忙得无暇于美、精得无暇于梦的世界——的安宁与餍足，绝望了。

===Original===

Having perceived at last the hollowness and futility of real things, Carter spent his days in retirement, and in wistful disjointed memories of his dream-filled youth. He thought it rather silly that he bother to keep on living at all, and got from a South American acquaintance a very curious liquid to take him to oblivion without suffering. Inertia and force of habit, however, caused him to defer action; and he lingered indecisively among thoughts of old times, taking down the strange hangings from his walls and refitting the house as it was in his early boyhood﻿—purple panes, Victorian furniture, and all.

With the passage of time he became almost glad he had lingered, for his relics of youth and his cleavage from the world made life and sophistication seem very distant and unreal; so much so that a touch of magic and expectancy stole back into his nightly slumbers. For years those slumbers had known only such twisted reflections of everyday things as the commonest slumbers know, but now there returned a flicker of something stranger and wilder; something of vaguely awesome immanence which took the form of tensely clear pictures from his childhood days, and made him think of little inconsequential things he had long forgotten. He would often awake calling for his mother and grandfather, both in their graves a quarter of a century.

Then one night his grandfather reminded him of the key. The gray old scholar, as vivid as in life, spoke long and earnestly of their ancient line, and of the strange visions of the delicate and sensitive men who composed it. He spoke of the flame-eyed Crusader who learnt wild secrets of the Saracens that held him captive; and of the first Sir Randolph Carter who studied magic when Elizabeth was queen. He spoke, too, of that Edmund Carter who had just escaped hanging in the Salem witchcraft, and who had placed in an antique box a great silver key handed down from his ancestors. Before Carter awaked, the gentle visitant had told him where to find that box; that carved oak-box of archaic wonder whose grotesque lid no hand had raised for two centuries.

===Chinese===

终于看透了实有之物的空洞与徒劳，卡特在退隐中度日，在惘然零落的回忆里重温他充满梦的少年。他觉得再费事活下去未免可笑，便从一个南美相识那里弄到一种很古怪的药水，要不受苦地领他入于遗忘。然而惰性和习惯的势力叫他一拖再拖；他在旧日之思里徘徊不决，把墙上的奇挂毯一幅幅取下，把宅子重新布置成他早年的样子——紫色的窗玻璃，维多利亚式的家具，一应俱全。

时光推移，他几乎庆幸自己拖了下来；因为他青年的遗物同他与世隔绝的状态，使生活和世故显得遥远而虚幻；以至一缕魔幻和期待，偷偷溜回了他夜间的睡眠。多年来那些睡眠只知道日常事物的扭曲倒影——同最寻常的睡眠一样——可如今有一种更怪更野的东西闪回：一种依稀可畏的临在，化作一帧帧紧绷而清晰的少年时代图景，叫他想起久已忘记的种种小事。他常常醒来喊着母亲和祖父，两位入土已二十五年的人。

随后一天夜里，祖父向他提起了那把钥匙。灰发老学者栩栩如生，恳切地长谈他们古老的血统，谈组成这血统的精微敏感之人所见的一切怪象。他谈到那位火眼金睛的十字军，在囚禁他的萨拉森人那里学了野秘术；谈到伊丽莎白女王在位时研习魔法的第一代兰道夫·卡特爵士。他还谈到埃德蒙·卡特——塞勒姆巫狱里险些吊死、逃脱后把先人传下的一柄巨大银钥匙放进一只古盒的那位。卡特醒来之前，这位温和的来客已经告诉他到哪里找那盒子；那只雕花的橡木盒，古奥的奇物，狰狞的盒盖两百年没有一只手掀过。

===Original===

In the dust and shadows of the great attic he found it, remote and forgotten at the back of a drawer in a tall chest. It was about a foot square, and its Gothic carvings were so fearful that he did not marvel no person since Edmund Carter had dared open it. It gave forth no noise when shaken, but was mystic with the scent of unremembered spices. That it held a key was indeed only a dim legend, and Randolph Carter’s father had never known such a box existed. It was bound in rusty iron, and no means was provided for working the formidable lock. Carter vaguely understood that he would find within it some key to the lost gate of dreams, but of where and how to use it his grandfather had told him nothing.

An old servant forced the carven lid, shaking as he did so at the hideous faces leering from the blackened wood, and at some unplaced familiarity. Inside, wrapped in a discolored parchment, was a huge key of tarnished silver covered with cryptical arabesques; but of any legible explanation there was none. The parchment was voluminous, and held only the strange hieroglyphs of an unknown tongue written with an antique reed. Carter recognized the characters as those he had seen on a certain papyrus scroll belonging to that terrible scholar of the South who had vanished one midnight in a nameless cemetery. The man had always shivered when he read this scroll, and Carter shivered now.

But he cleaned the key, and kept it by him nightly in its aromatic box of ancient oak. His dreams were meanwhile increasing in vividness, and though showing him none of the strange cities and incredible gardens of the old days, were assuming a definite cast whose purpose could not be mistaken. They were calling him back along the years, and with the mingled wills of all his fathers were pulling him toward some hidden and ancestral source. Then he knew he must go into the past and merge himself with old things, and day after day he thought of the hills to the north where haunted Arkham and the rushing Miskatonic and the lonely rustic homestead of his people lay.

===Chinese===

在大阁楼的尘与影里，他找到了它，藏得偏僻，忘在高柜抽屉的最里。它约一英尺见方，哥特式的雕花可怖之至，无怪自埃德蒙·卡特以后没人敢开。摇起来不作响，却带着一股记不起的香料的神秘气味。里面装着一把钥匙，这实在只是一线模糊的传说；兰道夫·卡特的父亲根本不知道有这么一只盒子。它绑着锈铁，也没有开那把狰狞之锁的门道。卡特依稀明白，他将在里面找到通往失落梦境之门的一把钥匙；可它在哪里用、怎么用，祖父一字未告。

一名老仆撬开了雕花的盖，撬时直打抖——为焦木上睨视的狰狞脸孔，也为某种说不清的似曾相识。里面，裹在一张变色的羊皮纸里，是一柄巨大的失去光泽的银钥匙，布满秘义的阿拉伯花饰；可读的解释一个字也没有。羊皮纸很长，只写着一种未知语言的怪符，用古旧的芦管笔写成。卡特认得这些字：他在南方那位可怕学者的一卷纸草上见过——那位学者一个午夜消失在无名墓地的。那人读这卷纸草时总是发抖；卡特此刻发抖了。

可他把钥匙擦净，每夜连着那芳香的古橡木盒带在身边。他的梦与此同时越来越鲜亮；虽然不再给他旧日的奇城和不可思议的花园，却显出一种确定的指向，其目的不会错认。它们在唤他逆着年头回去，携着他所有先人的意志，把他朝某个隐秘的、祖先的源头拉。于是他知道，他必须走进过去，把自己融进旧物；日复一日，他想着北边的群山——闹鬼的阿卡姆、奔流的米斯卡塔尼克和他一族孤零的农庄所在之地。

===Original===

In the brooding fire of autumn Carter took the old remembered way past graceful lines of rolling hill and stonewalled meadow, distant vale and hanging woodland, curving road and nestling farmstead, and the crystal windings of the Miskatonic, crossed here and there by rustic bridges of wood or stone. At one bend he saw a group of giant elms among which an ancestor had oddly vanished a century and a half before, and shuddered as the wind blew meaningly through them. Then there was the crumbling farmhouse of old Goody Fowler the witch, with its little evil windows and great roof sloping nearly to the ground on the north side. He speeded up his car as he passed it, and did not slacken till he had mounted the hill where his mother and her fathers before her were born, and where the old white house still looked proudly across the road at the breathlessly lovely panorama of rocky slope and verdant valley, with the distant spires of Kingsport on the horizon, and hints of the archaic, dream-laden sea in the farthest background.

Then came the steeper slope that held the old Carter place he had not seen in over forty years. Afternoon was far gone when he reached the foot, and at the bend halfway up he paused to scan the outspread countryside golden and glorified in the slanting floods of magic poured out by a western sun. All the strangeness and expectancy of his recent dreams seemed present in this hushed and unearthly landscape, and he thought of the unknown solitudes of other planets as his eyes traced out the velvet and deserted lawns shining undulant between their tumbled walls, the clumps of faery forest setting off far lines of purple hills beyond hills, and the spectral wooded valley dipping down in shadow to dank hollows where trickling waters crooned and gurgled among swollen and distorted roots.

===Chinese===

在秋天沉郁的火色里，卡特走上了记忆中的旧路，过起伏的山峦和石墙草场的优雅线条，过远谷和坡林，过弯路和偎窝的农舍，过米斯卡塔尼克晶亮的蜿蜒，时时被木桥石桥跨越。一个弯上，他看见一丛巨榆——一位先人在一个半世纪前古怪地消失在其中——风从榆树间意味深长地吹过，他打了个寒噤。然后是女巫古迪·富勒那坍败的农舍，小窗邪恶，大屋顶北坡几乎垂到地面。经过时他加快了车，直到爬上他母亲和外祖一门出生的山才松劲；白色老宅还骄傲地隔着路，望着那一幅屏息般可爱的全景：石坡与青谷，地平线上金斯波特远远的尖塔，极远处一线太古的、满载梦的海。

然后是更陡的坡，托着老卡特庄——他四十多年没见过的。到达山脚时午后已深；爬到半坡的弯上，他停下来，扫视铺展开的乡野——在西斜的太阳倾出的魔光的洪流里，金煌煌，圣化了。他近来一切梦的怪异与期待，仿佛都在这一片静穆而非人间的风景里；他的眼睛描摹着那些绒面而荒弃的草坪——在倾颓的墙间闪着微光，起伏不定——一簇簇仙林衬着远方紫山外之山的一线线，鬼影的林谷向下没入阴影，探进阴湿的洼地，那里涓涓的水在肿胀扭曲的根间吟哦、汩汩。

===Original===

Something made him feel that motors did not belong in the realm he was seeking, so he left his car at the edge of the forest, and putting the great key in his coat pocket walked on up the hill. Woods now engulfed him utterly, though he knew the house was on a high knoll that cleared the trees except to the north. He wondered how it would look, for it had been left vacant and untended through his neglect since the death of his strange great-uncle Christopher thirty years before. In his boyhood he had reveled through long visits there, and had found weird marvels in the woods beyond the orchard.

Shadows thickened around him, for the night was near. Once a gap in the trees opened up to the right, so that he saw off across leagues of twilight meadow and spied the old Congregational steeple on Central Hill in Kingsport; pink with the last flush of day, the panes of the little round windows blazing with reflected fire. Then, when he was in deep shadow again, he recalled with a start that the glimpse must have come from childish memory alone, since the old white church had long been torn down to make room for the Congregational Hospital. He had read of it with interest, for the paper had told about some strange burrows or passages found in the rocky hill beneath.

Through his puzzlement a voice piped, and he started again at its familiarity after long years. Old Benijah Corey had been his Uncle Christopher’s hired man, and was aged even in those far-off times of his boyhood visits. Now he must be well over a hundred, but that piping voice could come from no one else. He could distinguish no words, yet the tone was haunting and unmistakable. To think that “Old Benijy” should still be alive!

“Mister Randy! Mister Randy! Whar be ye? D’ye want to skeer yer Aunt Marthy plumb to death? Hain’t she tuld ye to keep nigh the place in the arternoon an’ git back afur dark? Randy! Ran﻿—dee!﻿ ﻿… He’s the beatin’est boy fer runnin’ off in the woods I ever see; haff the time a-settin’ moonin’ raound that snake-den in the upper timber-lot!﻿ ﻿… Hey, yew, Ran﻿—dee!”

===Chinese===

有什么叫他觉得，汽车不属于他要寻的国度；他把车撂在林边，把大钥匙放进外衣口袋，步行上山。林木此刻整个吞没了他，虽然他知道那房子在高冈上，除了北面都高过树木。他不知道它成了什么样子，自从三十年前他古怪的伯公克里斯托弗死后，它一直空置失修，全因他的疏忽。少年时他在那里一连数月流连忘返，在果园外的树林里觅得种种怪奇的珍宝。

影子在他四周加浓，因为夜近了。有一回，右手边树间豁开一道口子，他越过数里格暮色的草场望出去，看见了金斯波特中央山上公理会老教堂的尖塔：粉在白昼最后的红晕里，小圆窗的玻璃燃着反照的火。随后他又陷进浓荫，蓦地想起：那一瞥必是出于童年的记忆——因为那座白教堂早就拆了，给公理会医院让了地。他读过那条新闻，还饶有兴味，报上说岩石山体下发现了一些古怪的地洞或甬道。

一阵尖细的声音穿过他的惶惑，多年之后这嗓音的熟稔又叫他为之一震。老贝尼贾·科里曾是克里斯托弗伯公的雇工，在他少年来访的遥远年代就已经老了。如今必定过百了，可那尖嗓只可能出自他。字听不清，腔调却缠人而不容错认。想想「老本吉」竟然还活着！

「兰迪少爷！兰迪少爷！你哪儿去啦？想把你玛莎婶婶活活吓死呀？她不是嘱咐过，后晌要挨着家门口，天黑前回来吗？兰迪！兰——迪！……他是我见过的顶爱往林子里跑的娃儿，动不动就跑到上林木园那个蛇洞跟前发呆！……喂，你呀，兰——迪！」
